# 396. Tiling a Bigarray Transpose around Two Different Address Strides

```ocaml
open Bigarray
let transpose32 a b rows cols lda ldb =
  let ii = ref 0 in
  while !ii < rows do
    let jj = ref 0 in
    while !jj < cols do
      let ie = min rows (!ii + 32) in
      let je = min cols (!jj + 32) in
      for i = !ii to ie - 1 do
        let base = i * lda in
        for j = !jj to je - 1 do
          Array1.unsafe_set b (j * ldb + i)
            (Array1.unsafe_get a (base + j))
        done
      done;
      jj := !jj + 32
    done;
    ii := !ii + 32
  done
```

# 399. Deadline Retries in a Length-Framed Rust Receiver

Use Rust 1.85.0, edition 2021, and Tokio 1.43.0 with the single-thread runtime. The transport is a reliable ordered byte stream. Each record has a two-byte little-endian payload length, then exactly that many bytes; the length is 1 through 4. Payloads are arbitrary bytes and can themselves resemble headers. There is no framing marker, out-of-band length, reconnect, or transport rewind. `read_exact` follows this version's documented cancellation contract.

The receiver may impose a deadline while waiting, but a timeout must preserve the logical parser position so that retrying the same receiver eventually yields exactly the original records. A timeout is not permission to drop a record or reconnect. EOF before a record completes is a distinct error. The omitted caller retries after timeout and consumes a successful payload before asking for the next record. Only one receive operation exists at a time, and all arrays and stream objects remain alive.

```rust
use tokio::io::{AsyncRead, AsyncReadExt};
use tokio::time::{timeout, Duration};

#[derive(Debug)]
enum ReceiveError { Timeout, BadLength, Io(std::io::Error) }
struct Receiver<R> { io: R }
impl<R: AsyncRead + Unpin> Receiver<R> {
    async fn next(&mut self) -> Result<Vec<u8>, ReceiveError> {
        let mut header = [0u8; 2];
        match timeout(Duration::from_millis(10),
                      self.io.read_exact(&mut header)).await {
            Err(_) => return Err(ReceiveError::Timeout),
            Ok(Err(e)) => return Err(ReceiveError::Io(e)),
            Ok(Ok(_)) => {}
        }
        let n = u16::from_le_bytes(header) as usize;
        if !(1..=4).contains(&n) { return Err(ReceiveError::BadLength); }
        let mut body = vec![0u8; n];
        match timeout(Duration::from_millis(10),
                      self.io.read_exact(&mut body)).await {
            Err(_) => Err(ReceiveError::Timeout),
            Ok(Err(e)) => Err(ReceiveError::Io(e)),
            Ok(Ok(_)) => Ok(body),
        }
    }
}
```

You may choose when the transport supplies each byte; deadlines and poll outcomes must be consistent with that schedule. Concurrent reads or overlapping mutable borrows are outside scope.

Real-time fairness and exact timer granularity are not required conclusions.

# 400. An Exponential Pruning Threshold That Ignores the Number of Components

Rows are independent. The target is the real expression on represented scores and weights, with absolute error at most 2^-32 per row. The baseline precomputes log weights, shifts by a row maximum and uses several accumulation chains. The input t is the precomputed score-plus-log-weight row; its creation and rounding are part of the job cost.

~~~rust
fn shifted_logsum(t: &[f64]) -> f64 {
    assert!(!t.is_empty());
    let m = t.iter().copied().fold(f64::NEG_INFINITY, f64::max);
    let mut a = [0.0_f64; 4];
    let chunks = t.chunks_exact(4);
    let tail = chunks.remainder();
    for q in chunks {
        a[0] += (q[0] - m).exp();
        a[1] += (q[1] - m).exp();
        a[2] += (q[2] - m).exp();
        a[3] += (q[3] - m).exp();
    }
    let mut z = (a[0] + a[1]) + (a[2] + a[3]);
    for &v in tail { z += (v - m).exp(); }
    m + z.ln()
}
~~~

# 405. A Buffered Radix Pass with Too Many Simultaneously Open Buckets

Use C++14 and GCC 13.3.0 on Linux 6.12, targeting a two-socket x86-64 server with AVX2. A Tuple is exactly 16 bytes: a uint64_t payload identifier and a uint64_t precomputed hash. One stable radix pass partitions 2^24 tuples by b selected hash bits, where 4≤b≤14. Histogramming has already computed each worker's exclusive output ranges. Their starts are rounded to 64-byte boundaries; padding is excluded from logical output and included in space/traffic accounting. Threads have disjoint buffers and output ranges.

```cpp
struct Tuple { std::uint64_t id, hash; };
struct alignas(64) Lane { Tuple v[4]; };

void scatter(const Tuple* src, std::size_t n, unsigned shift,
             unsigned b, Lane* pending, unsigned* used,
             Tuple* dst, std::size_t* pos) {
    const std::uint64_t mask = (std::uint64_t(1) << b) - 1;
    for (std::size_t i = 0; i < n; ++i) {
        const auto k = unsigned((src[i].hash >> shift) & mask);
        const unsigned u = used[k];
        pending[k].v[u] = src[i];
        used[k] = u + 1;
        if (u == 3) {
            std::copy_n(pending[k].v, 4, dst + pos[k]);
            pos[k] += 4;
            used[k] = 0;
        }
    }
    for (unsigned k = 0; k < (1u << b); ++k) {
        std::copy_n(pending[k].v, used[k], dst + pos[k]);
        pos[k] += used[k];
        used[k] = 0;
    }
}
```

Auxiliary memory excluding input/output is limited to 32 MiB per socket.

# 413. A Slicing-by-Four CRC That Competes with Its Table Footprint

Use C++14, GCC 14.2 and Thumb-2 on a Cortex-M7 without a vendor CRC peripheral. The CRC is the reflected CRC32C recurrence with polynomial `0x82f63b78`, initial state all ones and final XOR all ones. `T[0][b]` is the state obtained by applying eight reflected polynomial steps to byte `b`; recursively `T[k+1][b]=(T[k][b]>>8)^T[0][T[k][b]&255]`. These immutable tables have already been built and their 4 KiB storage counts as working memory.

```cpp
#include <cstdint>
#include <cstring>
#include <cstddef>
uint32_t crc4(const uint8_t* p, size_t n, const uint32_t T[4][256]) {
    uint32_t c = ~uint32_t(0);
    while (n >= 4) {
        uint32_t w;
        std::memcpy(&w, p, 4);       // target is little-endian
        uint32_t z = c ^ w;
        c = T[3][z & 255] ^ T[2][(z >> 8) & 255]
          ^ T[1][(z >> 16) & 255] ^ T[0][z >> 24];
        p += 4; n -= 4;
    }
    while (n--) c = (c >> 8) ^ T[0][(c ^ *p++) & 255];
    return c ^ ~uint32_t(0);
}
```

# 416. Deferred Pixel Iteration after Frame Admission

Use CPython 3.13.2 and its standard `struct`, `memoryview`, and `zlib` modules. The contract for `admit` is snapshot-like: a successful result names the frame identifier and exactly the pixel sequence whose CRC was checked. Subsequent frame arrivals must not change an admitted result. No threads, native writes, or illicit buffer resizing are needed for this problem. The integer sum and pixel values are exact, and all lengths are even and at most eight.

```python
import struct
import zlib

class Camera:
    def __init__(self):
        self.storage = bytearray(8)
        self.pending = []

    def receive(self, frame_id, payload):
        n = len(payload)
        self.storage[:n] = payload
        return self.admit(frame_id, n, zlib.crc32(payload))

    def admit(self, frame_id, n, expected_crc):
        view = memoryview(self.storage)[:n]
        if zlib.crc32(view) != expected_crc:
            view.release()
            raise ValueError("crc")
        pixels = struct.iter_unpack("<H", view)
        self.pending.append((frame_id, pixels))
        del view
        return frame_id

    def integrate(self):
        frame_id, pixels = self.pending.pop(0)
        total = sum(value for (value,) in pixels)
        return frame_id, total
```

# 418. The Third Asynchronous Stage Evicts the Second Resident Block

```cpp
// s holds 2*2048 uint4 values; each thread copies eight objects.
for (int j=threadIdx.x; j<2048; j+=256)
  copy16(&s[j], &input[j]);
asm volatile("cp.async.commit_group;" ::: "memory");
for (int t=0; t<T; ++t) {
  if (t+1<T)
    for (int j=threadIdx.x; j<2048; j+=256)
      copy16(&s[((t+1)&1)*2048+j], &input[(t+1)*2048+j]);
  asm volatile("cp.async.commit_group;" ::: "memory"); // an empty group at the tail
  asm volatile("cp.async.wait_group 1;" ::: "memory");
  __syncthreads();
  for (int j=threadIdx.x; j<2048; j+=256)
```

# 421. Set-Prediction Matching with Empty Targets

Use Python 3.12 and NumPy 2.1. A set-prediction detector emits three named queries q0, q1, q2 and two real target objects A, B. Class probabilities and boxes are supplied immutable model outputs for this task; no neural network training run is required. There are three classes A, B and empty. Rows of `prob` sum to one, all entries are positive, and predictions use centre-x, centre-y, width, height normalized to the unpadded image. The matching cost for a real target is minus its predicted class probability plus twice the L1 box distance. An empty padding target has zero matching cost for every query. Matching is a one-to-one assignment between all three queries and the two real targets plus one empty target. Ties use lexicographically smallest query sequence in target order A, B, empty.

The supervised loss after matching uses negative log probability for all assigned targets, with empty-class weight 1/10, and twice L1 box distance only for real targets. The distinction between the matching cost and the supervised loss is intentional. Each box component is a rational multiple of 1/20. Matching assignments are treated as locally constant when differentiating away from an assignment boundary and away from an L1 kink.

```python
import numpy as np

def match(prob, boxes, target_classes, target_boxes):
    cost = np.empty((len(target_classes), len(boxes)))
    for t, cls in enumerate(target_classes):
        cost[t] = -np.log(prob[:, cls]) + 2.0 * np.abs(
            boxes - target_boxes[t]).sum(axis=1)
    chosen = np.argmin(cost, axis=1)
    return chosen, cost

def loss(prob, boxes, cls, target, chosen):
    out = 0.0
    for t, q in enumerate(chosen):
        out -= np.log(prob[q, cls[t]])
        out += 2.0 * np.abs(boxes[q]-target[t]).sum()
    return out

prob = np.array([[.48,.47,.05],[.45,.10,.45],[.10,.44,.46]])
boxes = np.array([[.5,.5,.2,.2],[.5,.5,.2,.2],[.5,.5,.2,.2]])
target_boxes = boxes[:2].copy()
```

Account for query and target permutations, including the deterministic tie rule.

# 422. Domain-Local Histograms and the Cost of Retiring Their Private Heaps

Use OCaml 5.2.0 native code on a 16-core Arm Neoverse N1 machine. The following baseline avoids an atomic update for every sample: it builds a private histogram in each domain, then performs a deterministic merge. `data` is an immutable ordinary OCaml int array. Counts and indices remain below the positive OCaml-int limit.

```ocaml
let local_hist data lo hi bins =
  let h = Array.make bins 0 in
  for i = lo to hi - 1 do
    let k = Array.unsafe_get data i in
    Array.unsafe_set h k (Array.unsafe_get h k + 1)
  done;
  h

let histogram data bins parts =
  let n = Array.length data in
  let jobs = Array.init parts (fun p ->
    let lo = p * n / parts and hi = (p+1) * n / parts in
    Domain.spawn (fun () -> local_hist data lo hi bins)) in
  let hs = Array.map Domain.join jobs in
  let out = Array.make bins 0 in
  Array.iter (fun h ->
    for k = 0 to bins - 1 do
      Array.unsafe_set out k
        (Array.unsafe_get out k + Array.unsafe_get h k)
    done) hs;
  out
```

~~~cpp
#include <cstdint>
#include <cstddef>

void count_blocks(const uint64_t* x, const uint64_t* y,
                  const uint64_t* vx, const uint64_t* vy,
                  std::size_t words4, uint64_t n[4],
                  uint64_t sx[4], uint64_t sy[4], uint64_t both[4]) {
    for (std::size_t j = 0; j < words4; j += 4) {
        for (unsigned k = 0; k != 4; ++k) {
            uint64_t v = vx[j+k] & vy[j+k];
            uint64_t a = x[j+k] & v, b = y[j+k] & v;
            n[k]    += __builtin_popcountll(v);
            sx[k]   += __builtin_popcountll(a);
            sy[k]   += __builtin_popcountll(b);
            both[k] += __builtin_popcountll(a & b);
        }
    }
}
~~~

Use CPython 3.12.14 to implement an offline CoAP/UDP Observe client under RFC 7641. One observation has a fixed endpoint, resource, and token for its lifetime.
```python
from dataclasses import dataclass

@dataclass
class Cache:
    serial: int
    stamp_ns: int
    expires_ns: int
    payload: bytearray

def notify(c, serial, now_ns, max_age_s, packet_payload):
    elapsed = now_ns - c.stamp_ns
    delta = (serial - c.serial) & 0xffffff
    newer = (0 < delta < 0x800000) or elapsed >= 128_000_000_000
    c.stamp_ns = now_ns
    c.expires_ns = now_ns + max_age_s * 1_000_000_000
    if newer:
        c.serial = serial
        c.payload = packet_payload
    return newer

def read(c, now_ns):
    return c.payload if now_ns < c.expires_ns else None
```

# 432. A Remote-Free Batch That Retains Sixty-Four Otherwise Empty Pages

Use Rust 1.85.0, edition 2021, on Linux 6.12 and a two-socket x86-64 server. An arena owner allocates fixed 64-byte objects from 64 KiB pages. Each producer has a preallocated 64-entry stash, with used initially zero and below 64 on entry to defer; each item represents one valid, not previously returned slot; the owner stays alive for the whole experiment, and page addresses are not reused until all their recorded frees have been consumed. Queue::publish is a supplied bounded, linearizable batch transfer: it copies records into owned preallocated queue storage, may wait under backpressure, and returns only after accepting the whole batch. Queue correctness is not in dispute.

```rust
#[derive(Clone, Copy)]
struct Free { page: u32, slot: u16 }

fn defer(stash: &mut [Free; 64], used: &mut usize,
         item: Free, queue: &Queue) {
    stash[*used] = item;
    *used += 1;
    if *used == 64 {
        stash.sort_unstable_by_key(|x| (x.page, x.slot));
        queue.publish(&stash[..]);
        *used = 0;
    }
}
```

# 433. Strict Atomic Updates for Signed-Batch Statistics

The observer can read the state only between completed calls. `audit` is a separate IORef used as an append-only logical log; its implementation is otherwise correct. The author treats `atomicModifyIORef'` as a transaction over computation, state replacement, and the returned result.

```haskell
{-# LANGUAGE ScopedTypeVariables #-}
import Control.Exception
import Data.IORef

data Stats = Stats { count :: !Int, total :: !Int }
  deriving (Eq, Show)

adjust :: IORef Stats -> IORef [Int] -> Int -> Int -> IO (Either ArithException Int)
adjust ref audit dn ds = do
  answer <- try $ atomicModifyIORef' ref $ \(Stats n s) ->
    let n' = n + dn
        s' = s + ds
        next = Stats n' s'
        mean = s' `div` n'
    in (next, mean)
  case answer of
    Left ex -> pure (Left ex)
    Right m -> do
      atomicModifyIORef' audit (\xs -> (m : xs, ()))
      pure (Right m)

fixture = do
  ref <- newIORef (Stats 2 10)
  audit <- newIORef []
  result <- adjust ref audit (-2) (-10)
  state <- readIORef ref
  entries <- readIORef audit
  pure (result, state, entries)
```

A binary output pixel is obtained by bilinearly sampling logits at its mapped original-image centre and testing logit>=0. Sampling uses border clamping only within the valid unpadded transformed image; points outside the original image are rejected. Interpolation then thresholding is the contract.

```typescript
type Image = { id: bigint; rev: number; w: number; h: number;
               bytes: Uint8Array };
type Embed = { owner: bigint; values: Float32Array };
let current: Image;
let embedding: Embed | undefined;
const cache = new Map<string, Promise<Embed>>();
async function select(img: Image) {
  current = img;
  const key = `${img.id}`;
  let p = cache.get(key);
  if (!p) { p = encode(img.bytes); cache.set(key, p); }
  embedding = await p;
}
async function point(x: number, y: number): Promise<Uint8Array> {
  const s = 1024 / Math.max(current.w, current.h);
  const logits = await decode(embedding!, [x*s, y*s]);
  return thresholdThenResize(logits, current.w, current.h);
}
```

# 441. The First Mismatch behind Four Speculative Vector Comparisons

Use C++17, GCC 14.2 and base SVE on a Neoverse N2. Two immutable disjoint byte arrays have equal length `n <= 2^24`. Return their first unequal index, or `n` if equal.
```cpp
#include <arm_sve.h>
#include <cstdint>
#include <cstddef>
size_t first_difference(const uint8_t* a, const uint8_t* b, size_t n) {
    for (size_t i=0; i<n; i += svcntb()) {
        svbool_t p = svwhilelt_b8(uint64_t(i), uint64_t(n));
        svuint8_t x = svld1_u8(p, a+i);
        svuint8_t y = svld1_u8(p, b+i);
        svbool_t bad = svcmpne_u8(p, x, y);
        if (svptest_any(p, bad)) {
            svbool_t before = svbrkb_z(p, bad);
            return i + svcntp_b8(p, before);
        }
    }
    return n;
}
```

A supplied parser returns a complete, validated PUBLISH packet with QoS 0, a decoded Topic Name, an optional Topic Alias, and a payload view into one reusable receive slab. UTF-8 validity and forbidden topic wildcards are checked before this kernel; the kernel must still enforce alias semantics. Topic Names are at most 64 UTF-8 bytes and payloads at most 512 bytes. There are no retained messages or shared subscriptions in this profile.

```typescript
type Packet = {
  topic: string;
  alias?: number;
  payload: Uint8Array;
};
type Pending = { alias?: number; topic: string; payload: Uint8Array };

class Gateway {
  aliases = new Map<number, string>();
  pending: Pending[] = [];
  receive(p: Packet) {
    if (p.alias !== undefined && p.topic.length !== 0)
      this.aliases.set(p.alias, p.topic);
    this.pending.push({ alias: p.alias, topic: p.topic,
                        payload: p.payload.subarray(0) });
  }
  dispatchOne() {
    const p = this.pending.shift();
    if (!p) return;
    const topic = p.alias === undefined ? p.topic : this.aliases.get(p.alias);
    if (topic !== undefined) commit(topic, p.payload);
  }
  reconnect(sessionPresent: boolean) {
    if (!sessionPresent) this.aliases.clear();
  }
}
```

`commit` synchronously appends an immutable `(topic, payload bytes)` row to an in-memory database. Its implementation copies its arguments before returning, so the issue is what it receives. The event loop is single-threaded, but any number of receive events can occur before a dispatch event. There is no JavaScript data race. The same gateway object is reused across successive Network Connections to the same authenticated Client Identifier, and the negotiated maximum received alias is 2 on each connection.

On connection A, receive topic `jobs/a`, alias 1, payload `01`; recycle the slab; then receive topic `jobs/b`, alias 1, payload `02`; only then dispatch both queued entries. A separate outbound publication sent by the server uses alias 1 for `status`; its mapping belongs to the opposite direction. Close A after its pending entries have either committed or been explicitly cancelled, establish connection B with Session Present true, and receive an empty Topic Name with alias 1 and payload `03`. In independent boundary fixtures, send alias 0, alias 3, a missing alias with an empty Topic Name, and a valid empty Topic Name after establishing alias 2 in that same direction and connection.

Determine the database rows and protocol decisions that should result, and compare them with the sketch. Explain why preserving an MQTT session does not preserve every piece of connection state, and why alias remapping may not retroactively change a queued publication's routing destination. A correct Topic Name string does not by itself fix a payload view whose underlying ArrayBuffer has been overwritten. TypeScript's static types and readonly properties do not add ownership or immutability to that backing storage.

Implement a repair that materializes a complete publication at receive admission, distinguishes inbound and outbound mappings, and attaches an unambiguous connection identity to deferred work. The queue holds at most eight publications. It may stop admitting work with a defined local resource failure, but it may not silently reroute or drop an admitted publication. Specify the fate of queued work on close and show how an old callback is prevented from consulting connection B's map. Use an explicit allocation model charging requested backing-buffer capacity plus 32 bytes per allocation; include three 4096-byte receive slabs, eight pending payloads, names, and mapping metadata in the bound.

Provide generated JavaScript, a replayable event transcript, and an object/ArrayBuffer identity trace before and after slab reuse. Exercise all boundary fixtures and show the appropriate distinction between invalid alias value and use of an unestablished alias. # 445. A Stable Radix Scatter Already Knows Each Lane’s Exact Rank

Use HIP C++17, ROCm 6.2.2, and one MI250X GCD (`gfx90a`, wave64). Sort `N=2^24` records with unsigned 32-bit keys and 32-bit payloads, stably in ascending key order. The input and output arrays are disjoint. The baseline performs eight four-bit LSD passes. Before each scatter, a histogram/prefix stage computes `base[d]`, the count of records in lower digits, and `wp[w][d]`, the count with digit d in all earlier physical waves. Both refer to the current pass input order and are exact.

```cpp
unsigned i=blockIdx.x*blockDim.x+threadIdx.x;
unsigned lane=threadIdx.x&63, w=i>>6;
unsigned key=keys[i], d=(key>>shift)&15u;
unsigned long long eq=~0ull;
#pragma unroll
for (unsigned b=0; b<4; ++b) {
  unsigned long long ones=__ballot((d>>b)&1u);
  eq &= ((d>>b)&1u) ? ones : ~ones;
}
unsigned long long before=(1ull<<lane)-1ull;
unsigned rank=__popcll(eq&before);
unsigned dst=base[d]+wp[w*16+d]+rank;
out_keys[dst]=key;
out_payload[dst]=payload[i];
```

All launches use block sizes divisible by 64, cover exactly N lanes, and all lanes execute the ballots. This avoids global scatter atomics and gives a stable rank. Explain which work is genuinely saved and which is moved into LDS, extra passes, synchronization, or index arithmetic. You may detect constant digits and skip their passes, but must include detection cost and prove stable order is unchanged. The workload families are uniform keys, all-equal keys, keys sharing their top 24 bits, and keys arranged so adjacent lanes have maximally different digits.

Derive temporary-space usage, histogram/prefix traffic, record bytes moved, and the number of ballot or cross-lane operations. Show why a lower pass count can still lose due to prefix footprint, register pressure, poor scatter sectors, or a residency cliff. A payload cannot be discarded or replaced by its position; stable ordering must apply to arbitrary payload bits and repeated keys.

The metric is complete device-resident sort latency including histogram, scan, scatter, detection, and initialization. Optimality is restricted to the implemented radix/grouping/prefix families and the stated input families. Extract AMDGPU ISA and identify ballot lowering, population counts, LDS accesses, scratch spills, and wave size. Use diagnostic transaction and occupancy counters with uninstrumented total-sort timings. Include a table of the cost crossover conditions, not only a fastest benchmark.

If hardware is unavailable, retain the analytical resource/traffic comparison and compilation artifacts where possible, and leave performance rankings conditional. # 449. A Bounded Heap Can Lose to Repeated Selection without Losing Asymptotics

Compile with OCaml 4.13.1 built with Flambda and ocamlopt -O3 on an Intel Cascade Lake server x86-64 core. The service maintains the K smallest distinct unsigned-31-bit keys from a stream. Inputs may repeat. Before each batch, a deduplication stage supplies a batch of distinct keys that are also distinct from all currently retained keys; its cost is outside this exercise and equal for all variants. The retained structure is a max heap in a fixed int array. The following hot operation replaces its root only when a new key qualifies.

```ocaml
let offer h used cap x =
  if used < cap then begin
    let p = ref used in
    while !p > 0 && h.((!p-1)/2) < x do
      h.(!p) <- h.((!p-1)/2);
      p := (!p-1)/2
    done;
    h.(!p) <- x;
    used + 1
  end else if x >= h.(0) then used
  else begin
    let p = ref 0 and moving = ref true in
    while !moving && 2 * !p + 1 < used do
      let l = 2 * !p + 1 in
      let r = l + 1 in
      let q = if r < used && h.(r) > h.(l) then r else l in
      if h.(q) <= x then moving := false
      else begin h.(!p) <- h.(q); p := q end
    done;
    h.(!p) <- x;
    used
  end
```

K is 1 through 65536; a batch has 64 through 2^22 keys. `cap=K>0`, `used` is initially in [0,K], and the prefix is a valid max heap. The heap must represent the exact K smallest seen keys, or all keys if fewer than K have been seen. No intermediate query occurs within a batch, and the final result is requested as a sorted ascending array. Extra memory beyond input and output is at most 24K bytes. All batch processing, copying, selection and final sorting are charged.

The baseline uses the root as a cheap rejection threshold and moves a hole rather than swapping on every sift step. Assess its optimality for mostly rejected batches, decreasing input, and phases that repeatedly change the threshold. Construct a buffered selection alternative and a crossover rule; buffering may defer updates only because the contract excludes mid-batch queries. Derive a worst-case work bound and an output correctness invariant, rather than relying on expected behavior of randomized quickselect. If randomized selection is used, state the expectation and include a deterministic fallback.

Trace the heap worker through Flambda and native assembly. Determine whether bound checks are removed, whether the local refs escape, and whether branchless child selection improves or worsens the load dependency chain. Inspect the selection loop as carefully as the heap loop: fewer comparisons can produce more stores, branch misses or full-buffer passes. Give a fixture in which K fits L1 but path-dependent loads still limit the heap, and one in which the rejection branch is almost perfect.

Submit both implementations, exact tests for K=1 and boundary batch sizes, a proof for the selected set and sorted output, and a breakdown of comparisons, input passes and cache-line traffic. Optimality is limited to the heap and your explicitly specified bounded-buffer selection family, for declared arrival regimes. Include the cost of exposing sorted output so that a heap is not penalized or favored by a different interface. ```ocaml

```ocaml
  = "validate_tile"
exception Bad_tile of string
```

```c
#include <stdlib.h>
#include <caml/mlvalues.h>
#include <caml/memory.h>
#include <caml/alloc.h>
#include <caml/callback.h>
#include <caml/fail.h>
CAMLprim value validate_tile(value fn, value tile) {
    CAMLparam2(fn, tile);
    CAMLlocal2(r, answer);

    CAMLreturn(answer);
}
```

# 453. A Bandwidth Sweep That Keeps Rebuilding the Same Spectrum

Use CPython 3.12.7, NumPy 2.1.3 and SciPy 1.14.1 on an EPYC 9654 socket. An exact input histogram h on a cycle of length L=2^k, 12<=k<=20, consists of nonnegative integer counts with total between one and 2^40. Define p=h/sum(h) in real arithmetic. For each smoothing time t, return exp(tD)p, where (Dp)_j=p_{j-1}-2p_j+p_{j+1} with cyclic indices. Thus the target is the discrete heat-kernel smoother, not an approximation to a continuous Gaussian density. Times are binary64 in [2^-12,L^2] and arrive either as an arbitrary list of up to 512 values or as t0+j delta with nonnegative represented t0,delta. Output arrays may be streamed one at a time.

The baseline caches both the input spectrum and the generator eigenvalues, then batches inverse transforms:

~~~python
import numpy as np
from scipy.fft import rfft, irfft

def heat_sweep(hist, times, batch=8):
    n = len(hist)
    p = hist.astype(np.float64) / int(sum(map(int, hist)))
    hp = rfft(p)
    k = np.arange(n // 2 + 1, dtype=np.float64)
    eigen = -4.0 * np.sin(np.pi * k / n)**2
    for lo in range(0, len(times), batch):
        t = np.asarray(times[lo:lo + batch], dtype=np.float64)
        spec = hp[None, :] * np.exp(t[:, None] * eigen[None, :])
        yield irfft(spec, n=n, axis=1)
~~~

State a reset or correction policy and charge its transforms and exponentials.

The numerical contract is l1 error at most 2^-25 against the mathematical pmf for every returned time. struct V { float x,y; };
```cpp
V sample(const V* f, int stride, int w, int h, float x, float y);
V lift(const V* f, int stride, int x, int y) {
    float u = float(x) / 8.0f;
    float v = float(y) / 8.0f;
    V z = sample(f, stride, 80, 60, u, v);
    return {z.x / 8.0f, z.y / 8.0f};
}
size_t corr_offset(int sy, int sx, int ty, int tx,
                   int level, int target_w, int target_h) {
    int source_w = 80 >> level;
    return (((size_t(sy)*source_w + sx)*target_h + ty)*target_w + tx);
}
void write_flow(V* out, int out_stride, int x, int y, V z) {
    out[y*out_stride+x] = z;
}
```

# 459. A Cache-Sized Top-k Pass Whose Candidate Pool Becomes the Working Set

Use CPython 3.12.4 and NumPy 2.1.3 on Linux 6.12, with the exact wheel/build and its CPU dispatch features recorded. Target an x86-64 AVX2 server. There are N≤2^26 rows and 1≤k≤min(N,4096). keys is a contiguous uint64 array. A token packs a 32-bit score in the high half and (0xffffffff−row_id) in the low half, so all tokens are distinct and larger tokens order higher scores first, then smaller row identifiers. Payloads are separate 1 KiB records. They are fetched only after the final k row identifiers are known.

```python
import numpy as np

def top_rows(keys, k, block=65536):
    local = []
    for lo in range(0, keys.size, block):
        a = keys[lo:lo + block]
        t = min(k, a.size)
        ix = np.argpartition(a, a.size - t)[-t:]
        local.append(a[ix])
    pool = np.concatenate(local)
    ix = np.argpartition(pool, pool.size - k)[-k:]
    winners = np.sort(pool[ix])[::-1]
    return (np.uint64(0xffffffff) -
            (winners & np.uint64(0xffffffff))).astype(np.uint32)
```

This is a hierarchical exact selection: it avoids sorting the full input and constrains each local partition to a contiguous slice. A review calls it optimal because no excluded local token can enter the global top k and the payload is never moved during selection.

A native C++ or Rust helper is allowed, but its build, dispatch, call overhead, and temporary storage must be part of the result.

# 466. Four Delta Chains inside a Longer Scalable Vector

Use Rust 1.85.0, edition 2021, with the AArch64 Advanced SIMD intrinsics below. The input contains `n` unsigned 16-bit deltas, where `n` is a multiple of four and at most `2^24`.
```rust
use std::arch::aarch64::*;
pub fn decode4(d: &[u16], out: &mut [u32], seed: [u32; 4]) -> [u32; 4] {
    assert_eq!(d.len(), out.len());
    assert_eq!(d.len() % 4, 0);
    let mut last = seed;
    unsafe {
        let mut s = vld1q_u32(seed.as_ptr());
        for i in (0..d.len()).step_by(4) {
            let z = vld1_u16(d.as_ptr().add(i));
            s = vaddw_u16(s, z);
            vst1q_u32(out.as_mut_ptr().add(i), s);
        }
        vst1q_u32(last.as_mut_ptr(), s);
    }
    last
}
```

# 468. Read-Only Pixel Views through a Java Decoder

Use Java SE 21, OpenJDK jdk-21+35, and heap ByteBuffers. A sensor format uses little-endian fields: a four-byte unsigned frame identifier, a two-byte pixel count, then that many unsigned 16-bit pixel values. Counts are 1 through 4. The frame has exactly `6 + 2*count` bytes. CRC verification is supplied as a correct raw-byte predicate and succeeds for the fixture. There is one thread, the original bytes remain unchanged, and every buffer stays alive; native memory reclamation and data races are excluded.

The decoder returns the original unsigned identifier and exact integer sum of the pixels. Its API intentionally returns a read-only payload view so a later stage cannot alter the packet through that view. The author believes that setting the received buffer to little endian establishes a property inherited by all its views. The code performs several view operations because an earlier parser version needed to preserve its cursor.

```java
import java.nio.ByteBuffer;
import java.nio.ByteOrder;
record Packet(long id, ByteBuffer pixels) {}

final class Decoder {
    static boolean crcOK(ByteBuffer raw) { return true; } // stipulated checker
    static Packet admit(ByteBuffer raw) {
        raw.order(ByteOrder.LITTLE_ENDIAN);
        int start = raw.position();
        long id = Integer.toUnsignedLong(raw.getInt());
        int n = Short.toUnsignedInt(raw.getShort());
        if (n < 1 || n > 4 || raw.remaining() != 2*n)
            throw new IllegalArgumentException("length");
        if (!crcOK(raw.duplicate().position(start)))
            throw new IllegalArgumentException("crc");
        ByteBuffer payload = raw.slice();
        ByteBuffer frozen = payload.asReadOnlyBuffer();
        return new Packet(id, frozen);
    }
    static long integrate(Packet packet) {
        ByteBuffer p = packet.pixels().duplicate();
        long sum = 0;
        while (p.hasRemaining()) sum += Short.toUnsignedInt(p.getShort());
        return sum;
    }
}
```

Explain why read-only status and byte order are independent properties, and why a duplicate can preserve cursor state while resetting an interpretation property.

Repair both admission and integration. Audit applying `.order(LITTLE_ENDIAN)` only to `payload`, only before `asReadOnlyBuffer`, and only once when receiving the original packet. Choose an API that makes byte order explicit whenever a ByteBuffer view is created, or return a typed immutable representation whose interpretation can no longer be reset by a caller's duplicate. Keep the zero-copy payload option available and preserve the original raw buffer's externally specified cursor behavior: after admission it must point just after the header, whether validation succeeds or fails after the header has been read.

Now add one field of IEEE binary32 pixels in an independent format variant. The byte order problem must be tested on raw bits, including 0x3f800001 and a quiet NaN payload. Do not replace exact-bit requirements by approximate numeric comparisons, and do not treat the sum of NaNs as an informative byte-order oracle. Specify how the format variant exposes the decoded bit patterns without relying on a particular NaN payload surviving arithmetic.

Build a table-driven oracle for all one-pixel inputs from `{0,1,0x0102,0x8000,0xff00,0xffff}` and a few multi-pixel frames, checking identifiers, bytes, cursor state, and sums. Inspect the pinned ByteBuffer API/source template for each relevant view method. If a JDK 21 compiler is unavailable, distinguish a portable Java source harness and Python byte-order oracle from an actually executed Java test.

# 471. Quantized Boxes Save Cache Lines and Lengthen Every Traversal Step

```cpp

  unsigned long long a=(unsigned long long)span*q.lo;
  unsigned long long b=(unsigned long long)span*(unsigned(q.hi)+1u);
  return make_uint2(origin+unsigned(a>>16),
```

```haskell
import Data.List (transpose, maximumBy)
import Data.Ord (comparing)

type Matrix = [[Double]]
scaleRows :: Matrix -> Matrix
scaleRows = map (\xs -> let s = sum xs in map (/ s) xs)

scaleCols = transpose . scaleRows . transpose
```

# 475. A Probe Fingerprint That Avoids Key Loads but Extends the Miss Chain

Use TypeScript 5.3.3 targeting ES2022 and Node.js 20.11.1 on an AMD Zen 4 x86-64 core. The hash table is immutable during a lookup batch. It uses parallel Uint32Array keys/values and a Uint8Array fingerprint array, with zero denoting an empty slot. Capacity is a power of two at most 2^24, load factor is at most 7/8, and insertion used linear probing with the same hash. Key zero is ordinary; occupancy is carried only by fingerprints.

```typescript
function hash(x: number): number {
  x = Math.imul(x ^ (x >>> 16), 0x7feb352d);
  x = Math.imul(x ^ (x >>> 15), 0x846ca68b);
  return (x ^ (x >>> 16)) >>> 0;
}
function get(keys: Uint32Array, vals: Uint32Array,
             tag: Uint8Array, key: number): number {
  const h = hash(key), mask = keys.length - 1;
  const t = 1 + ((h >>> 24) % 255);
  let p = h & mask;
  for (;;) {
    const c = tag[p];
    if (c === 0) return -1;
    if (c === t && keys[p] === key) return vals[p];
    p = (p + 1) & mask;
  }
}
```

All arrays have the same capacity, the table is well formed, keys and queries are uint32 values, and values are below 2^31 so −1 is an unambiguous miss. Each successful key has exactly one slot. No deletion or tombstone exists. Batches contain 32 through 2^20 queries, including mostly misses and adversarially selected long clusters. The supplied hash is deterministic, so an average-case claim must declare a distribution; load factor alone does not bound cluster length. The output must preserve query order.

Assess that claim and implement a batch alternative that pipelines several independent probes or scans a small group of adjacent tags. Extra scratch is at most 24 bytes per active query for at most 64 active queries, plus the output. You may not resize or rehash the table, convert to a different index, use WebAssembly or call native code. Any group load or packed-tag trick must remain within JavaScript's exact numeric and typed-array semantics.

If a group encounters both a matching tag and an earlier empty slot, explain which positions may still be inspected and which matches may be returned. Produce a counterexample to an incorrect group rule. Derive both worst-case probe work and a conditional expected-work model; do not present an empirical average as a load-factor theorem.

Inspect V8 optimized machine code for the hash arithmetic, modulo fingerprint conversion, tag/key load dependence and table bounds. Determine whether pipelining increases outstanding misses or merely adds state spills and dispatcher branches. Design a pair of equal-probe-count workloads that differs in tag/key locality, and a separate experiment distinguishing branch misses from dependent cache misses. Include setup, output restoration, warm-up and any deoptimization recovery in the declared accounting.

Optimality is scoped to linear-probe lookup scheduling over this fixed layout under the 64-query state limit.
```kotlin
data class Pio(val valid: Long, val preferred: Long,
               val a: Boolean, val l: Boolean, val p: Boolean)
data class Address(var validUntil: Long, var preferredUntil: Long,
                   var live: Boolean = true)

fun apply(a: Address, pio: Pio, now: Long, routerLifetime: Long,
          timers: MutableList<Pair<Long, () -> Unit>>) {
    val remaining = maxOf(0L, a.validUntil - now)
    a.validUntil = now + minOf(remaining, pio.valid)
    a.preferredUntil = now + pio.preferred
    timers.add(a.validUntil to { a.live = false })
    if (routerLifetime == 0L || !pio.l) a.live = false
}
```

# 481. Interleaved Tridiagonal Systems with No Work between Python Calls

Use CPython 3.12.7 and NumPy 2.1.3, with any proposed extension compiled by Clang 18.1.8. Compare an Intel Xeon Platinum 8480+ socket with Graviton3. Solve B independent real tridiagonal systems of length n, 32<=n<=2^14 and 1<=B<=4096, with nB<=2^24. Coefficients are stored as n-by-B C-contiguous arrays, so different systems at the same equation index are adjacent. Lower and upper coefficients lie in [-1,1]; each diagonal is at least 1+|lower|+|upper| and at most 4. The first lower and last upper are zero. Right-hand sides lie in [-1,1]. The matrices are reused for 1 through 1024 RHS batches.

The factorization is already outside the timed solve, reciprocals are cached, and the hot arrays are interleaved for vector operations across systems:

~~~python
import numpy as np

def factor(lower, diagonal, upper):
    n, batch = diagonal.shape
    inv = np.empty_like(diagonal)
    cp = np.empty_like(upper)
    inv[0] = 1.0 / diagonal[0]
    cp[0] = upper[0] * inv[0]
    for i in range(1, n):
        inv[i] = 1.0 / (diagonal[i] - lower[i] * cp[i-1])
        cp[i] = upper[i] * inv[i]
    return inv, cp

def solve_factored(lower, inv, cp, rhs):
    z = np.empty_like(rhs)
    z[0] = rhs[0] * inv[0]
    for i in range(1, len(rhs)):
        z[i] = (rhs[i] - lower[i] * z[i-1]) * inv[i]
    for i in range(len(rhs)-2, -1, -1):
        z[i] -= cp[i] * z[i+1]
    return z
~~~

```ocaml
let lookup runs key =

  let rec visit i =

    else

  visit 0
```

```python
from collections import defaultdict
from math import sqrt

def report(images):
    bins = defaultdict(list)
    accepted = []
    for image in images:
        for confidence, correct in image:
            b = int(confidence * 10)
            bins[b].append((confidence, correct))
            if confidence >= .9:

    stderr = sqrt(p*(1-p)/len(accepted))
```

```rust
pub fn intersection_bits(a: &[u64], b: &[u64]) -> u64 {
    assert_eq!(a.len(), b.len());
    let (mut s0, mut s1, mut s2, mut s3) = (0u64,0u64,0u64,0u64);
    let mut i = 0;
    while a.len() - i >= 4 {
        s0 += (a[i]   & b[i]).count_ones() as u64;
        s1 += (a[i+1] & b[i+1]).count_ones() as u64;
        s2 += (a[i+2] & b[i+2]).count_ones() as u64;
        s3 += (a[i+3] & b[i+3]).count_ones() as u64;
        i += 4;
    }
    let mut sum = s0+s1+s2+s3;
    while i < a.len() {
        sum += (a[i] & b[i]).count_ones() as u64;
        i += 1;
    }
    sum
}
```

Final draining uses the same operation. Allocation and pipeline creation precede timing.

```rust
for (job, words) in jobs.iter().enumerate() {
    let s = &mut slots[job % 3];
    if s.pending { retire(&device, s); }
    queue.write_buffer(&s.input, 0, bytemuck::cast_slice(words));
    let mut enc = device.create_command_encoder(&Default::default());

    s.pending = true;
}
```

# 501. Coefficient Leases across Buffer Resizing

Use TypeScript 5.7.3 compiled to ES2024 and ECMAScript 2024's resizable ArrayBuffer semantics. Execute on a Node.js version supporting those semantics; record the actual engine separately from the language specification. One thread owns all objects. A protocol decoder lends a fixed-length byte view to a later vision stage, while a capacity manager may shrink and regrow the underlying ArrayBuffer. No transfer, SharedArrayBuffer, worker, native code, or concurrent mutation occurs.

The public contract says an admitted four-byte little-endian coefficient remains stable until its lease is released. The manager treats unchanged buffer identity and restored byte length as evidence that an old lease is again valid. Bytes removed by shrinking are not externally saved. New storage from growth follows the stipulated ECMAScript zero-initialization rule. The code intentionally uses indexed typed-array reads, not DataView methods, because the author expects out-of-bounds reads to fail similarly.

```typescript
type Lease = { readonly view: Uint8Array; readonly generation: number };
class Slab {
  readonly backing = new ArrayBuffer(8, { maxByteLength: 16 });
  generation = 0;
  lease(): Lease {
    return { view: new Uint8Array(this.backing, 4, 4),
             generation: this.generation };
  }
  trimAndRestore(): void {
    this.backing.resize(4);
    this.backing.resize(8);
  }
  coefficient(x: Lease): number {
    if (x.generation !== this.generation || x.view.length !== 4)
      throw new Error("expired");
    return ((x.view[0] | 0) + 256 * (x.view[1] | 0)
      + 65536 * (x.view[2] | 0) + 16777216 * (x.view[3] | 0));
  }
}
const slab = new Slab();
new Uint8Array(slab.backing).set([9,9,9,9,2,1,0,0]);
const old = slab.lease();
slab.trimAndRestore();
const answer = slab.coefficient(old);
```

Explain why restoring the shape does not restore the overwritten logical generation.

Your answer must not invoke C-style undefined behavior for an ordinary JavaScript indexed read that yields undefined and is subsequently coerced.

Retaining original bytes through a copy is permitted only if its storage is counted; total owned backing and copy capacity may not exceed 32 bytes.

# 502. Unrolling Varint Decoding across the Boundary between Bytes and Values

Use TypeScript 4.9.5 targeting ES2020 and Node.js 16.20.2 on an Arm Neoverse N1 core.
```typescript
function decode(src: Uint8Array, out: Uint32Array, n: number): number {
  let p = 0;
  for (let k = 0; k < n; ++k) {
    const a = src[p++];
    if (a < 128) { out[k] = a; continue; }
    const b = src[p++];
    let x = (a & 127) | ((b & 127) << 7);
    if (b < 128) { out[k] = x; continue; }
    const c = src[p++];
    x |= (c & 127) << 14;
    if (c < 128) { out[k] = x; continue; }
    const d = src[p++];
    out[k] = (x | (d << 21)) >>> 0;
  }
  return p;
}
```

# 522. A Saturating FIR Whose Wide Accumulators Cannot Be Narrowed Early

Translation targets: AArch64 Advanced SIMD and POWER9 VSX.

```cpp
int16_t clip(int64_t s) {
    s += 16384;
    int64_t q=s>=0?s/32768:-((-s+32767)/32768);
    return q>32767?32767:q< -32768?-32768:(int16_t)q;
}
void fir(int16_t*y,const int16_t*x,const int16_t*h,size_t n){
    for(size_t i=0;i<n;++i){
        int64_t p=0,q=0;
        for(size_t k=0;k<8;k+=2){
            p+=(int64_t)x[i+k]*h[k];
            q+=(int64_t)x[i+k+1]*h[k+1];
        }

    }
}
```

# 551. Stable Byte Compaction with Overlapping Wide Stores

Use C++20, GCC 14.2, Linux x86-64 System V. Input arrives as 32-byte blocks and one u32 selection mask per block; bit j retains input byte j. Output concatenates retained bytes in original order. The baseline uses an SSSE3 shuffle table for each eight-byte piece. For mask m, ctrl[m] contains the selected indices 0..7 in increasing order, followed by 0x80 bytes; each row has 16 bytes. The 4096-byte table is read-only and aligned to 16. The routine deliberately makes overlapping stores:

```cpp
#include <immintrin.h>
#include <cstdint>
#include <cstddef>
std::size_t compact32(const unsigned char* src, std::uint32_t mask,
                       unsigned char* dst, const __m128i* ctrl) {
    std::size_t used=0;
    for (unsigned k=0; k!=4; ++k) {
        unsigned m=(mask>>(8*k))&255u;
        __m128i x=_mm_loadl_epi64((const __m128i*)(src+8*k));
        __m128i y=_mm_shuffle_epi8(x,_mm_load_si128(ctrl+m));
        _mm_storeu_si128((__m128i*)(dst+used),y);
        used+=(unsigned)__builtin_popcount(m);
    }
    return used;
}
```

The output allocation has n+16 writable bytes for n input bytes, and bytes beyond the returned logical length are scratch whose final values do not matter. Input and output do not overlap. These conditions are part of the API: use them to prove the baseline stores are safe, rather than treating the deliberate overstore as an incidental bug. Input n is a multiple of 32 in [0,2^24]. Mask storage is disjoint, and no input or mask can change during the call.

# 555. A Three-Row Stencil That Still Writes Every Intermediate Image

Use C++17, GCC 14.2 and a Cortex-M7 with 32 KiB of DTCM available to this task. The two full images reside in ordinary external RAM. Each is `H*W` unsigned 16-bit cells, with `64 <= H,W <= 1024`; both boundary frames are permanently zero. One time step replaces each interior cell by the sum of itself and its four axial neighbors modulo `2^16`. Perform `T` steps, `1 <= T <= 8`, and return only the final image. The two arrays are disjoint, and the caller does not observe intermediate states.

```cpp
#include <cstdint>
#include <cstring>
#include <utility>
// W <= 1024; rows is in DTCM, a and b in external RAM.
uint16_t* evolve(uint16_t* a, uint16_t* b, unsigned H,
                 unsigned W, unsigned T, uint16_t rows[3][1024]) {
    for (unsigned t=0; t<T; ++t) {
        std::memcpy(rows[0], a,   2*W);
        std::memcpy(rows[1], a+W, 2*W);
        for (unsigned y=1; y+1<H; ++y) {
            std::memcpy(rows[(y+1)%3], a+(y+1)*W, 2*W);
            const uint16_t* u=rows[(y-1)%3];
            const uint16_t* m=rows[y%3];
            const uint16_t* d=rows[(y+1)%3];
            for (unsigned x=1; x+1<W; ++x)
                b[y*W+x] = uint16_t(uint32_t(u[x])+d[x]
                                  +m[x-1]+m[x]+m[x+1]);
        }
        std::swap(a,b);
    }
    return a;
}
```

```cpp
                          const unsigned* weight, const unsigned* feature,
                          unsigned* out, unsigned* head, unsigned jobs) {
  __shared__ unsigned j;
  unsigned t=threadIdx.x; // exactly 256 threads

    __syncthreads();
```

# 562. Specializing Sparse Rows without Turning a Loop into an Instruction-Cache Problem

```haskell
{-# LANGUAGE BangPatterns #-}
applyRows :: U.Vector Int -> U.Vector Int -> U.Vector Double
          -> U.Vector Double -> U.Vector Double
applyRows rp col val x = U.generate (U.length rp - 1) row
  where
    row r = loop (U.unsafeIndex rp r)
                 (U.unsafeIndex rp (r+1)) 0
    loop !j !end !s
      | j == end = s

              !a = U.unsafeIndex val j
              !v = U.unsafeIndex x c
          in loop (j+1) end (s + a*v)
```

# 565. A Matrix-Free Newton Step That Streams the Training Matrix Twice per Iteration

Use CPython 3.12.7, NumPy 2.1.3, SciPy 1.14.1 and OpenBLAS 0.3.28 on a two-socket EPYC 9654 system. The diagonal weights lie in [2^-30,1/4], lambda lies in [2^-20,1] times max(1,||X||_F^2), and G has one through sixteen columns with finite binary64 entries in [-1,1]. The baseline avoids forming H, reuses the weighted diagonal and provides a matrix-matrix callback for a block iterative method:

~~~python
import numpy as np
from scipy.sparse.linalg import LinearOperator

def hessian_operator(X, w, lam):
    d = X.shape[1]
    def mv(v):
        v = np.asarray(v, dtype=np.float64).reshape(-1)
        z = X @ v
        z *= w
        return X.T @ z + lam * v
    def mm(V):
        Z = X @ V
        Z *= w[:, None]
        return X.T @ Z + lam * V
    return LinearOperator((d, d), matvec=mv, matmat=mm,
                          dtype=np.dtype(np.float64))
~~~

# 568. Local Graph Shards That Still Exchange the Same Labels Every Round

Use Rust 1.70.0, edition 2021, opt-level=3, Linux 6.12, and a two-socket x86-64 server. An optional second target is an AArch64 server exposing two NUMA nodes. An immutable undirected simple graph has n≤2^26 vertices and m≤2^29 edges. CSR rows are assigned to sockets by contiguous vertex ranges. Each worker owns a disjoint, cache-line-separated slice of next; cur is immutable until a barrier swaps the buffers. Initially cur[v]=v. Repeating the following kernel to convergence returns the minimum original identifier in each connected component.

```rust
fn relax_shard(base: usize, off: &[usize], edge: &[u32],
               cur: &[u32], next: &mut [u32]) -> bool {
    let mut changed = false;
    for (i, dst) in next.iter_mut().enumerate() {
        let v = base + i;
        let mut best = cur[v];
        for &u in &edge[off[v]..off[v + 1]] {
            best = best.min(cur[u as usize]);
        }
        changed |= best != cur[v];
        *dst = best;
    }
    changed
}
```

# 576. A Marginal Prior across Tangent-Origin Changes

Use C++20 and GCC 13.3. A sliding-window estimator minimizes a frozen linear least-squares objective E(delta)=1/2 delta^T H delta+g^T delta+c. Its state is ordered by stable variable IDs. The tangent coordinate delta=x-xbar is Euclidean for this exercise; no Lie-group approximation is hidden in the notation. Variables to eliminate are m and retained variables are r.
```cpp
struct Prior {
    Matrix H;
    Vector g;
    Vector anchor;
    double constant;
    std::vector<unsigned long long> ids;
};
Prior eliminate(Matrix Hmm, Matrix Hmr, Matrix Hrr,
                Vector gm, Vector gr, Vector anchor, double c) {
    Matrix X = solve(Hmm, Hmr);
    Vector y = solve(Hmm, gm);
    return {Hrr - transpose(Hmr)*X,
            gr - transpose(Hmr)*y,
            anchor, c - 0.5*dot(gm,y), {}};
}
void rebase(Prior& p, const Vector& current) {
    p.anchor = current;
}
double value(const Prior& p, const Vector& x) {
    Vector d = x - p.anchor;
    return 0.5*dot(d,p.H*d) + dot(p.g,d) + p.constant;
}
```

```haskell
import Data.Word
run :: [Word32] -> [Word32] -> Word32
run xs ys = go 0 1 xs ys
  where
    go s _ [] [] = s
```

# 579. A Specialized Bit-Unpacker Whose Code Size Competes with Its Data Savings

Use C++17, GCC 14.2 and SVE2 on a Neoverse N2. A block contains 128 unsigned integers and a public width `B` in {3,5,7,9,12,16}. Groups of four integers are packed into `ceil(4*B/8)` little-endian bytes, with zero padding in unused high bits of the final byte. Groups do not share bits. The output must contain the 128 decoded integers as unsigned 32-bit words. Blocks and outputs are disjoint; the input ends exactly after the last group. The width is validated before dispatch.

```cpp
#include <cstdint>
#include <cstring>
template<unsigned B>
void unpack128(const uint8_t* p, uint32_t* out) {
    static_assert(B>=1 && B<=16, "width");
    const uint64_t mask = (uint64_t(1)<<B)-1;
    const unsigned bytes = (4*B+7)/8;
    for (unsigned g=0; g<32; ++g) {
        uint64_t w=0;
        std::memcpy(&w, p+g*bytes, bytes); // little-endian target
        out[4*g  ] = uint32_t( w        & mask);
        out[4*g+1] = uint32_t((w>>B)     & mask);
        out[4*g+2] = uint32_t((w>>(2*B)) & mask);
        out[4*g+3] = uint32_t((w>>(3*B)) & mask);
    }
}
```

# 582. A Register Top-Sixteen Filter Spills Before It Saves the Sort

A fixed warp merge network then keeps the sixteen smallest from the 32 sorted lane lists. The merge is exact and charged; this excerpt shows the optimized thresholded local filter.

```cpp
unsigned long long best[16];
#pragma unroll
for (int k=0; k<16; ++k) best[k]=~0ull;

      best[k]=min(old,v);
      v=max(old,v);
```

# 583. QUIC Acknowledgements and Recovery across Packet Spaces

Use C++23 with GCC 13.3.0 and an offline QUIC version 1 sender. Apply RFC 9000 and RFC 9002, incorporating verified erratum 7539 for the RTT variance update order. Packet authentication and ACK-frame syntax checking are supplied; an ACK event includes its authenticated packet-number space, disjoint acknowledged ranges, decoded acknowledgement delay, and a local monotonic reception time. It is not sufficient for the largest packet number to look plausible in some other space.

```cpp
enum class Space { Initial, Handshake, Application };
struct Sent {
    Space space;
    std::uint64_t pn, sent_us;
    bool eliciting;
    std::shared_ptr<const std::vector<std::byte>> bytes;
};
struct Recovery {
    std::map<std::uint64_t, Sent> sent;
    double smooth = 100000, variation = 20000, minimum = 70000;
    void remember(Sent p) { sent.insert_or_assign(p.pn, std::move(p)); }
    void ack(Space space, std::uint64_t pn, std::uint64_t now,
             std::uint64_t delay) {
        auto it = sent.find(pn);
        if (it == sent.end()) return;
        double r = double(now - it->second.sent_us) - double(delay);
        smooth = 0.875 * smooth + 0.125 * r;
        variation = 0.75 * variation + 0.25 * std::abs(smooth - r);
        sent.erase(it);
    }
};
```

# 586. A Parallel Prefix Scan That Spends Its Work Budget Copying Strict Results

Use GHC 9.6.6, vector 0.13.1.0 and parallel 3.2.2.0 on a single-socket 16-core AMD Zen 3 system. Build with `-O2 -threaded`, and record the RTS capabilities, affinity and heap settings. The baseline partitions an unboxed vector, computes local scans in parallel, scans block totals, and adds each block's offset.

```haskell
{-# LANGUAGE BangPatterns #-}
import Data.Word
import qualified Data.Vector.Unboxed as U
import Control.Parallel.Strategies

scanBlocks :: Int -> U.Vector Word64 -> U.Vector Word64
scanBlocks b xs =
  let n = U.length xs
      chunks = [U.slice i (min b (n-i)) xs | i <- [0,b..n-1]]
      local v = let w = U.scanl' (+) 0 v
                in (U.tail w, U.last w)
      pieces = withStrategy (parList rdeepseq) (map local chunks)
      offsets = init (scanl (+) 0 (map snd pieces))
  in U.concat (zipWith (\o (v,_) -> U.map (+o) v) offsets pieces)
```

The block size b is positive. Input length is 0 through 2^27, every input word is defined, and output element i is the sum of elements 0 through i modulo 2^64. There are no exceptions from input evaluation, callbacks or concurrent mutations. The timed operation ends only when the complete result is available. Input allocation is outside timing; all result allocation, scheduling, offset work, copying and collection caused by the call are inside. The allowed additional live payload is 24N bytes plus 1 MiB of scheduler metadata, excluding the immutable N-word input and runtime's documented fixed reserve.

```c
#include <sqlite3.h>
#include <stdint.h>
#include <stdlib.h>

static void destroy_table(void *p) { free(p); }

static void calibrated(sqlite3_context *cx, int argc, sqlite3_value **argv) {
    (void)argc;
    const unsigned char *name = sqlite3_value_text(argv[0]);
    const unsigned char *bytes = sqlite3_value_blob(argv[1]);
    int n = sqlite3_value_bytes(argv[1]);

}
```

~~~cpp
#include <vector>
#include <utility>

struct Node { Factor qr; int left = -1, right = -1; };
struct Tree { std::vector<Node> nodes; int root; };

Tree tsqr(std::vector<Panel>& panels) {
    Tree tree;
    std::vector<int> active;
    for (auto& panel : panels) {
        active.push_back(int(tree.nodes.size()));
        tree.nodes.push_back({factor_panel(panel), -1, -1});
    }
    while (active.size() > 1) {
        std::vector<int> next;
        for (std::size_t j = 0; j < active.size(); j += 2) {
            if (j + 1 == active.size()) { next.push_back(active[j]); continue; }
            int l = active[j], r = active[j+1];
            Factor f = merge_qr(tree.nodes[l].qr.R(), tree.nodes[r].qr.R());
            next.push_back(int(tree.nodes.size()));
            tree.nodes.push_back({std::move(f), l, r});
        }
        active.swap(next);
    }
    tree.root = active.front();
    return tree;
}
~~~

```rust
struct Sim { s: f64, r: Mat3, t: Vec3 }
struct Camera { c: Mat3, d: Vec3, vel: Vec3, cov_v: Mat3 }

fn apply(g: &Sim, x: Vec3) -> Vec3 { g.s * (g.r*x) + g.t }
fn merge(src: &Map, g: &Sim) -> Map {

    for x in &mut out.points { *x = apply(g, *x); }

    out
}
```

The current implementation performs a bottom-up then top-down full semijoin reduction on the path. Its hot reducer copies surviving rows with a merge scan, avoiding random hash probes:

```cpp
struct Row { std::uint32_t key, other; std::uint64_t row_id; };
std::vector<Row> reduce(std::span<const Row> rows,
                        std::span<const std::uint32_t> allowed) {
    std::vector<Row> out;
    out.reserve(rows.size());
    std::size_t j = 0;
    for (const Row& r : rows) {
        while (j < allowed.size() && allowed[j] < r.key) ++j;
        if (j == allowed.size()) break;
        if (allowed[j] == r.key) out.push_back(r);
    }
    return out;
}
```

rows is sorted by key, allowed is sorted and unique, and projections/reindexing between reducer steps are correct and charged. After reduction, indexed enumeration produces the final tuples. Entries 0 and 1 have been legitimately evicted. Entries 2–5 remain, with names x2, x3, x4, x5 and values a, b, c, d respectively; each occupies 35 bytes, for 140 bytes total. Known Received Count is 2. The following kernel handles the decoder's cancellation instruction:

```rust
use std::collections::BTreeMap;
struct Section { required: u64, references: Vec<u64> }
struct Encoder {
    known: u64,
    outstanding: BTreeMap<u64, Vec<Section>>,
    refs: BTreeMap<u64, usize>,
}
impl Encoder {
    fn cancelled(&mut self, stream: u64) {
        if let Some(sections) = self.outstanding.remove(&stream) {
            for section in sections {
                self.known = self.known.max(section.required);
                for index in section.references {
                    *self.refs.get_mut(&index).unwrap() -= 1;
                }
            }
        }
    }
    fn potentially_blocked(&self, required: u64) -> bool {
        required > self.known
    }
}
```

The encoder sends a field section on request stream 0 with Required Insert Count 6 and a reference to absolute entry 5. The decoder blocks it while its insert count is 2, then abandons stream 0 and sends Stream Cancellation. Deliver that cancellation to the encoder before any remaining encoder-stream insertion bytes. # 603. Eight SIMD Decimal Digits inside a Parser with Exact Error Order

The helper below reads exactly eight bytes, rejects any non-ASCII digit, and converts eight digits through paired multiply-add reductions. It is already a specialized SIMD decimal kernel:

```rust
use core::arch::x86_64::*;
#[target_feature(enable = "ssse3,sse4.1")]
unsafe fn digits8(p: *const u8) -> Option<u32> {
    let x = _mm_loadl_epi64(p.cast::<__m128i>());
    let d = _mm_sub_epi8(x, _mm_set1_epi8(b'0' as i8));
    let ok = _mm_cmpeq_epi8(_mm_min_epu8(d,_mm_set1_epi8(9)), d);
    if (_mm_movemask_epi8(ok) & 255) != 255 { return None; }
    let pair = _mm_maddubs_epi16(d, _mm_set1_epi16(0x010a));
    let quad = _mm_madd_epi16(pair, _mm_set1_epi32(0x00010064));
```

# 607. A Segmented Scan Whose Fast Carry Belongs Only to the First Segment

Use C++17, GCC 14.2 and RV64GC+V 1.0. The input arrays contain `n <= 2^24` words `x[i]` and head flags `h[i]` in {0,1}; output is a segmented inclusive sum modulo `2^32`. At a head, the sum restarts at `x[i]`; otherwise it continues the previous sum. The incoming carry is supplied even when `h[0]=0`, and `n=0` returns that carry. Arrays are disjoint. The following block kernel already uses a parallel doubling scan, with snapshots to make every level independent.

```cpp
#include <array>
#include <cstdint>
uint32_t block(const uint32_t* x, const uint32_t* h,
               uint32_t* out, unsigned b, uint32_t carry) {
    // 1 <= b <= 64
    std::array<uint32_t,64> s{}, f{}, ns{}, nf{};
    for (unsigned j=0; j<b; ++j) { s[j]=x[j]; f[j]=h[j]; }
    if (!f[0]) s[0] += carry;
    for (unsigned d=1; d<b; d*=2) {
        for (unsigned j=0; j<b; ++j) {
            ns[j]=s[j]; nf[j]=f[j];
            if (j>=d) {
                if (!f[j]) ns[j] += s[j-d];
                nf[j] |= f[j-d];
            }
        }
        s=ns; f=nf;
    }
    for (unsigned j=0; j<b; ++j) out[j]=s[j];
    return s[b-1];
}
```

# 608. Revision Integration through a Rust Watch Channel

Use Rust 1.85.0, Tokio 1.43.0, and one cooperative executor thread. A task runs until an awaited future returns Pending; there is no task preemption or inline producer callback between ordinary instructions. A worker may skip a superseded revision, but it must integrate any revision it chooses at most once. Integration appends `(revision, mass)` to an audit vector; this is a logical result, not a lossy diagnostic log. Each mass is an integer 0 through 100.

The `gate` future is a controllable scheduler boundary used by an asynchronous GPU-readback simulator. The simulator stores no borrowed data and cannot call the worker inline. The producer may publish during this gate. The watch channel starts at revision 0; the worker is not required to integrate that initial value. After the last publication the producer remains alive until the worker has reached the supplied test termination condition, so channel closure is not the decisive issue.

```rust
use tokio::sync::watch;
use std::sync::Arc;

#[derive(Clone, Debug)]
struct Snapshot { revision: u64, mass: u32, pixels: Arc<[u8]> }

async fn worker(mut rx: watch::Receiver<Snapshot>,
                mut gate: impl FnMut() -> std::pin::Pin<Box<dyn std::future::Future<Output=()>>>)
                -> Vec<(u64,u32)> {
    let mut audit = Vec::new();
    while audit.len() < 2 {
        if rx.changed().await.is_err() { break; }
        gate().await;
        let snapshot = rx.borrow().clone();
        let result = snapshot.mass; // bounded exact readback model
        audit.push((snapshot.revision, result));
    }
    audit
}
```

# 614. Camera-Time Updates in a Cached IMU Preintegrator

Use Python 3.12 and NumPy 2.1. To isolate timing and uncertainty, consider one translational axis with no rotation or gravity. An IMU supplies acceleration a_k that is exactly constant on each half-open interval[t_k, t_{k+1}), with times in seconds. The accelerometer bias b is constant over a camera interval. State order is(position, velocity), and propagation over duration h is p'=p+vh+(a_k-b)h²/2, v'=v+(a_k-b)h. The noise model is additive continuous white acceleration with spectral density q in square metres per cubic second, independent between disjoint time intervals. Bias uncertainty is a separate constant random variable with supplied variance s_b² and is independent of that white noise.

Camera exposure timestamps are c0=0.0015 and c1=0.0055 seconds. IMU time equals camera time plus unknown offset delta. Therefore preintegration covers[c0+delta, c1+delta], clipping the first and last IMU intervals. The sample boundaries are 0,0.001,...,0.008 and acceleration values are[0,1,3,2,-1,4,0,2] metres per second squared. Delta is restricted to[-0.001,0.001], b to[-1/4,1/4], q=1/100, and s_b²=1/400. The cache initially uses delta=0, b=0 and is then queried at delta=0.00025, b=1/8.

```python
import numpy as np
cache = {}
def preintegrate(frame_ids, imu, delta, bias, q):
    if frame_ids in cache:
        return cache[frame_ids]
    p = v = 0.0
    P = np.zeros((2,2))
    for a, h in imu:       # caller supplies whole sample intervals
        p += v*h + .5*(a-bias)*h*h
        v += (a-bias)*h
        F = np.array([[1.,h],[0.,1.]])
        Q = np.diag([q*h*h, q*h])
        P = F @ P @ F.T + Q
    cache[frame_ids] = (p, v, P)
    return cache[frame_ids]
```

Its name and OCaml declaration are:

```ocaml
open Bigarray
external gather_block :
  (float, float64_elt, c_layout) Array1.t ->
  (int32, int32_elt, c_layout) Array1.t -> int -> int ->
  (float [@unboxed])
  = "gather_block_bytecode" "gather_block_native" [@@noalloc]

let gather data indices block =
  let n = Array1.dim indices in
  let rec loop i acc =
    if i = n then acc
    else
      let len = min block (n - i) in
      let s = gather_block data indices i len in
      loop (i + len) (acc +. s)
  in
  loop 0 0.
```

```haskell
import Data.Word
import qualified Data.ByteString as B

data Sig = Sig { inception :: Word32, expiration :: Word32,
                 originalTTL :: Word32, signatureTTL :: Word32 }
data Ticket = Ticket B.ByteString Sig Word32 Word32

timeOK :: Word32 -> Sig -> Bool
timeOK now s = inception s <= now && now <= expiration s

prepare :: Word32 -> Word32 -> Sig -> B.ByteString -> Maybe Ticket
prepare wall rrTTL sig canonical
  | timeOK wall sig = Just (Ticket canonical sig rrTTL wall)
  | otherwise      = Nothing

publish :: Word64 -> Ticket -> Bool -> Maybe (B.ByteString, Word64)
publish mono (Ticket bytes sig rrTTL checkedAt) verified
  | verified = Just (bytes, mono + fromIntegral life)
  | otherwise = Nothing
  where life = minimum [rrTTL, signatureTTL sig, originalTTL sig]
```

# 622. A Level-Scheduled Triangular Solve with a Barrier for Every Thin Frontier

Use Rust 1.85.0, edition 2021, and Rayon 1.10.0 on one EPYC 9654 socket. L is a unit lower-triangular CSR matrix with n<=2^20 rows, at most 64 stored strict-lower entries per row and increasing column indices. Every stored coefficient is nonzero; zero entries are omitted, so every loaded predecessor has a graph edge. Every row has sum of absolute strict-lower coefficients at most 1/2. Entries are finite binary64. A topological level partition of the row dependency graph is supplied and validated; an edge j->i exists for every stored nonzero L_ij. Solve Lx=b for 1 through 16 right-hand sides, repeatedly for the same pattern and values. RHS entries lie in [-1,1].

The one-RHS baseline parallelizes each frontier without unsafe shared mutable access. Its temporary vector is retained at the maximum frontier size between calls.

~~~rust
use rayon::prelude::*;

fn solve_levels(levels: &[Vec<usize>], rp: &[usize], ci: &[u32],
                a: &[f64], b: &[f64], x: &mut [f64], temp: &mut [f64]) {
    for rows in levels {
        temp[..rows.len()].par_iter_mut().zip(rows.par_iter())
            .for_each(|(out, &i)| {
                let mut s = b[i];
                for p in rp[i]..rp[i+1] {
                    s = (-a[p]).mul_add(x[ci[p] as usize], s);
                }
                *out = s;
            });
        for (&i, &v) in rows.iter().zip(temp.iter()) { x[i] = v; }
    }
}
~~~

# 628. Calibration Migration through Python’s SQLite Context Manager

Use CPython 3.13.2 with SQLite 3.49.1. The connection explicitly selects `autocommit=sqlite3.LEGACY_TRANSACTION_CONTROL` and isolation level `DEFERRED`. It is used by one thread, with no other database connection, crash, busy handler, trigger, or concurrent writer. The initial database has one calibration row `(revision=0, gain=10)` and an empty audit table. These initial contents have been committed.

An update should install revision 1 with gain 20 and one matching audit row, or leave the database at its initial state if validation fails. The validator deliberately raises a Python ValueError; SQLite exposes that callback failure as the documented SQL error. The in-memory cache is updated only after the context manager returns normally. All SQL text is fixed trusted program text, so injection and quoting are outside scope.

```python
import sqlite3

con = sqlite3.connect(":memory:", isolation_level="DEFERRED",
                     autocommit=sqlite3.LEGACY_TRANSACTION_CONTROL)
con.executescript("""
CREATE TABLE calibration(revision INTEGER, gain INTEGER);
INSERT INTO calibration VALUES(0,10);
CREATE TABLE audit(revision INTEGER, gain INTEGER);
""")
cache = {"revision": 0, "gain": 10}

def validate(gain):
    if gain == 20:
        raise ValueError("calibration rejected")
    return 1
con.create_function("validate", 1, validate)

def migrate():
    with con:
        con.execute("UPDATE calibration SET revision=1, gain=20")
        con.executescript("""
          INSERT INTO audit SELECT revision,gain FROM calibration;
          SELECT validate(gain) FROM calibration;
        """)
    cache.update(revision=1, gain=20)
```

# 631. Deferred Carries in a Vectorized Small-Integer Convolution

Use C++14, GCC 14.2, Linux x86-64 System V, AVX2. A nonnegative integer is represented by n little-endian radix-2^15 digits, each stored in the low bits of a u64. Here n is a multiple of four in [4,256]. The following multiplication stage accumulates exact convolution coefficients before carry propagation. c has 2n zero-initialized u64 entries and is disjoint from both inputs. The baseline already uses four parallel unsigned products and deferred carries:

```cpp
#include <immintrin.h>
#include <cstddef>
#include <cstdint>
void coefficients(const std::uint64_t* a, const std::uint64_t* b,
                  std::uint64_t* c, std::size_t n) {
    for (std::size_t i=0; i<n; ++i) {
        __m256i ai=_mm256_set1_epi64x((long long)a[i]);
        for (std::size_t j=0; j<n; j+=4) {
            __m256i bj=_mm256_loadu_si256((const __m256i*)(b+j));
            __m256i cv=_mm256_loadu_si256((const __m256i*)(c+i+j));
            cv=_mm256_add_epi64(cv,_mm256_mul_epu32(ai,bj));
            _mm256_storeu_si256((__m256i*)(c+i+j),cv);
        }
    }
}
```

```haskell
sub (x,y,z) (a,b,c) = (x-a,y-b,z-c)

                       == sq (sub (ys!!i) (ys!!j))
```

# 637. Eight Branchless Trie Steps through an Oversized Routing Node

Use C++17, GCC 14.2 and a Neoverse N2. A static IPv4 routing table has at most 65,536 prefixes of arbitrary lengths 0 through 32 and 16-bit route values.
```cpp
#include <cstdint>
const uint32_t NONE = ~uint32_t(0);
struct alignas(64) Node {
    uint32_t next[16];
    uint32_t match;
};
uint32_t route(const Node* nodes, uint32_t address, uint32_t def) {
    uint32_t p=1, best=def;
    for (unsigned level=0; level<8; ++level) {
        unsigned nibble=(address >> (28-4*level)) & 15;
        p=nodes[p].next[nibble];
        uint32_t m=nodes[p].match;
        best = m==NONE ? best : m;
    }
    return best;
}
```

```text

40 02 04 02 01 fc 00           AS_SEQUENCE containing AS 64512
40 03 04 c0 00 02 01           NEXT_HOP 192.0.2.1
```

```cpp
struct Update { PrefixList withdrawn, announced; ByteSpan attrs; };
void on_update(Peer peer, Update u) {
    auto root = current.load();
    auto next = std::make_shared<Rib>(*root);
    for (auto p : u.withdrawn) next->erase({peer, p});
    for (auto p : u.announced)
        next->insert_or_assign({peer, p}, RouteView{u.attrs});
    current.store(next);
    if (!attributes_ok(u.attrs)) {
        session_reset(peer);
        return;
    }
    input_pool.release(u.attrs.owner());
```

# 642. A Packed Column Predicate Must Earn Its PCIe Crossing

Use C++17 with Clang 18.1.8 on a Xeon Gold 6338 host and CUDA 12.4.1 on an A100 PCIe GPU. A column has `N` unsigned integers, `2^20 <= N <= 2^30`, packed contiguously into little-endian 32-bit words at width b, where 9<=b<=17. Bit i*b starts value i; a zero padding word makes the final two-word load legal. The host snapshot is immutable. Query output is a bitmap of `lo <= value < hi` and the exact 64-bit sum of selected values. The bitmap must preserve original row identities.

The device baseline fuses unpacking and predicate evaluation, uses a warp ballot for 32 bitmap bits, and emits one partial sum per warp. It never materializes a decompressed column. Full warps cover the timed N, which is a multiple of 32.

```cpp
unsigned i=blockIdx.x*blockDim.x+threadIdx.x;
unsigned long long bit=(unsigned long long)i*b;
unsigned p=unsigned(bit>>5), off=unsigned(bit&31);
unsigned long long pair=(unsigned long long)packed[p]
                       |((unsigned long long)packed[p+1]<<32);
unsigned v=unsigned(pair>>off)&((1u<<b)-1u);
bool keep=(lo<=v && v<hi);
unsigned mask=__ballot_sync(0xffffffffu,keep);
unsigned sum=__reduce_add_sync(0xffffffffu,keep?v:0u);
if ((threadIdx.x&31)==0) {
  bitmap[i>>5]=mask;
  partial[i>>5]=sum;
}
```

For larger H, you may retain a device representation, but charge upload and construction. Every bitmap returns to host memory and every sum is consumed there. # 646. Worker Registration and Masking in a Haskell Service

Use GHC 9.10.1, base 4.20.0.0, and `-threaded +RTS -N2`. A service starts short-lived image workers and keeps a registry of live worker identifiers for shutdown. The parent enters `launch` unmasked. Parent cancellation and allocation failure are excluded during this bounded launch; the worker may receive one asynchronous cancellation only after its identifier has been returned to a client. Registry operations are nonthrowing apart from ordinary asynchronous interruption and hold their MVar only for bounded pure updates.

The worker body must begin in `Unmasked`, may run up to eight bounded calibration steps, and must execute cleanup exactly once on success, synchronous exception, or permitted cancellation. A cleanup callback is allowed to execute immediately because a user job can finish without blocking. Neither masking nor use of one capability is a promise that a forked child cannot run before its parent continues.

```haskell
import Control.Concurrent
import Control.Exception
import qualified Data.Set as S

type Registry = MVar (S.Set ThreadId)
insertWorker reg tid = modifyMVar_ reg (pure . S.insert tid)
removeWorker reg tid = modifyMVar_ reg (pure . S.delete tid)

launch :: Registry -> IO () -> IO ThreadId
launch reg job = mask_ $ do
  tid <- forkFinally job $ \_ -> do
    me <- myThreadId
    removeWorker reg me
  insertWorker reg tid
  pure tid

jobFixture :: MVar MaskingState -> IO ()
jobFixture seen = do
  state <- getMaskingState
  putMVar seen state
  pure ()
```

# 647. A Delta Worklist Whose Deduplication Becomes the Dominant Algorithm

Use OCaml 5.2.0 native code on an Arm Neoverse N2 core. Consider a monotone dataflow solver on a directed graph. The following is the complete hot propagation step; a supplied deque stores vertex indices without allocating per operation.

```ocaml
let propagate succ masks facts queued push u =
  let fu = Array.unsafe_get facts u in
  let es = Array.unsafe_get succ u in
  let ms = Array.unsafe_get masks u in
  for j = 0 to Array.length es - 1 do
    let v = Array.unsafe_get es j in
    let old = Array.unsafe_get facts v in
    let add = fu land Array.unsafe_get ms j in
    let now = old lor add in
    if now <> old then begin
      Array.unsafe_set facts v now;
      if not (Array.unsafe_get queued v) then begin
        Array.unsafe_set queued v true;
        push v
      end
    end
  done
```

The required result is the least fixed point extending the initial seeds, with no requirement on worklist order. Execution is single-domain; concurrency is not a permissible shortcut.

The forward image-formation contract is implicit: v=f(Y-vy(t0+tau v))/Z+cy, followed by u=f(X-vx(t0+tau v))/Z+cx. This simplified physical model is exact for the question.

For all admitted points, Z is in [1,8], |vx|,|vy| are at most 1, and tau is in [0,1/1000]. Therefore the implicit row denominator is separated from zero. Observed coordinates(uo, vo) have independent equal-variance noise in pixel units. The optimizer's objective is one half the sum of squared differences between the explicitly predicted(u, v) and observed(uo, vo), with fixed weights. It estimates X, Y and tau while Z, t0, vx, vy are supplied per observation. There are at most 64 tracks and eight frames.

```ocaml
let predict_at_observed_row ~x ~y ~z ~vx ~vy ~t0 ~tau ~vo =
  let t = t0 +. tau *. vo in
  (320. +. 400. *. (x -. vx *. t) /. z,
   240. +. 400. *. (y -. vy *. t) /. z)
let residual obs state =
  let u,v = predict_at_observed_row
    ~x:state.x ~y:state.y ~z:obs.z ~vx:obs.vx ~vy:obs.vy
    ~t0:obs.t0 ~tau:state.tau ~vo:obs.vo in
  [| u -. obs.uo; v -. obs.vo |]
let tau_column obs =
  [| -.400. *. obs.vx *. obs.vo /. obs.z;
     -.400. *. obs.vy *. obs.vo /. obs.z |]
```

# 657. A Buffered Priority Queue That Rebuilds the Winner Path for Every Record

Use CPython 3.12.4 on Linux 6.12 and an x86-64 AVX2 server. A priority queue is represented by at most 4096 immutable sorted runs of 16-byte (uint64 key,uint64 insertion_sequence) records. The pair gives a total order and sequence numbers do not wrap. A batch of insertions may create a new run between drain calls; no insertion overlaps a drain. Every active run has a buffered current head in heap. Run.next_after_head advances past that head and reads an 8 KiB page when necessary, returning the new head or None at exhaustion.

```python
import heapq

def drain(heap, runs, count):
    answer = []
    for _ in range(count):
        key, seq, r = heap[0]
        answer.append((key, seq))
        nxt = runs[r].next_after_head()
        if nxt is None:
            heapq.heappop(heap)
        else:
            heapq.heapreplace(heap, (nxt[0], nxt[1], r))
    return answer
```

Each drain is guaranteed to request no more records than exist. Run buffers and heap capacity are reserved; output-list allocation remains part of the measured drain. The baseline uses heapreplace to combine removal and replacement and reads storage in pages rather than issuing one read per record. A review argues that its O(log R) winner selection and page buffering make further algorithmic work pointless compared with faster storage.
