It may inspect per-page minimum/maximum metadata and prefetch pages, but metadata generation and storage count toward costs. Total auxiliary RAM, excluding returned records, is 64 MiB; active pages must remain valid while compared, and the same page cannot be counted as both free scratch and an outstanding I/O buffer. The queue must remain correct after arbitrary new runs are inserted between drains.

Exploit intervals during which one run is known to precede every competing head, if profitable. Prove when an entire prefix may be emitted without a winner-tree update per record. Show how an adversarial interleaving of runs removes that advantage. Future insertions are unknown and cannot be included in the current drain's ordering proof. A compaction strategy is allowed only if its reads, writes, and delay are charged to the same operation trace.

```cpp
    std::uint64_t allocation_id;

bool newer(const Lsa& a, const Lsa& b) {
    if (a.sequence != b.sequence) return a.sequence > b.sequence;
    if (a.checksum != b.checksum) return a.checksum > b.checksum;
```

# 662. Eight Tiny SIMD Functions behind One Indirect Dispatch

```cpp
#include <immintrin.h>
alignas(32) extern unsigned char perm[8][32], xmask[8][32];
template<unsigned K>
void kernel(const unsigned char* in, unsigned char* out) {
    __m256i x=_mm256_loadu_si256((const __m256i*)in);
    x=_mm256_shuffle_epi8(x,_mm256_load_si256((const __m256i*)perm[K]));
    x=_mm256_xor_si256(x,_mm256_load_si256((const __m256i*)xmask[K]));
    _mm256_storeu_si256((__m256i*)out,x);
}
using Fn=void(*)(const unsigned char*,unsigned char*);
const Fn family[8]={kernel<0>,kernel<1>,kernel<2>,kernel<3>,
                    kernel<4>,kernel<5>,kernel<6>,kernel<7>};
void apply(unsigned mode,const unsigned char* in,unsigned char* out) {
    family[mode](in,out); // 0 <= mode < 8
}
```

```ocaml
  Hashtbl.replace cache id (w, e);
  e

  let dead = ref [] in
  Hashtbl.iter (fun id (w, _) ->
    if Weak.get w 0 = None then dead := id :: !dead) cache;
  List.iter (Hashtbl.remove cache) !dead

    let e = build id in consume e;
    Gc.full_major (); sweep ()
```

# 667. A DFA Fast Path That Skips Letters but Serializes Every Exception

There are at most 16 distinct transition columns across the alphabet: two bytes are equivalent only if their next states agree for every starting state. #include <cstdint>
```cpp
#include <cstddef>

Result run(const uint8_t* p, size_t n, const uint8_t go[16][256],
           const uint8_t accept[16], uint32_t s) {
    uint32_t hits=0;
    while (n>=8) {
        uint8x8_t x=vld1_u8(p);
        uint8x8_t m=vand_u8(vcge_u8(x,vdup_n_u8('a')),
                           vcle_u8(x,vdup_n_u8('z')));

    return {s,hits};
}
```

# 672. Forward and Reverse Compositing for Projected Gaussians

Use C++20 for a scalar reference and, if available, CUDA 12.4.1 on sm_80 for a tiled implementation. A trained scene representation supplies projected 2D Gaussian splats. Projection of a 3D covariance is the local affine approximation Sigma2=J C Sigma3 C^T J^T at the splat centre; it is not claimed to be exact projection of the full 3D density. In this task each positive definite Sigma2, centre, colour and opacity is supplied. Per-pixel alpha values computed from them are supplied to the compositor after clipping into[0,1], so the compositing problem is independently testable without evaluating an exponential.

The reference order is increasing positive camera-centre depth, with increasing splat ID breaking equal-depth ties. This declared order is used for every pixel, even where another physical visibility model would order overlapping extended primitives differently. For colour channels in [0,1] and background b in [0,1], the pixel is C=sum_i T_i alpha_i c_i+T_end b, with T_0=1 and T_{i+1}=T_i(1-alpha_i). At most 64 splats affect any pixel. Exact alpha=1 is allowed, and the contract requests the one-sided derivative with respect to alpha at that boundary while holding order and projected geometry fixed.

```cpp
struct S { double alpha, colour; };
double forward(const std::vector<S>& s, double bg,
               double& finalT) {
    double T=1, C=0;
    for (auto a:s) { C += T*a.alpha*a.colour; T *= 1-a.alpha; }
    finalT=T;
    return C+T*bg;
}
std::vector<double> backward(const std::vector<S>& s,
                             double bg, double finalT) {
    std::vector<double> g(s.size());
    double T=finalT, suffix=bg;
    for (size_t i=s.size(); i-- > 0;) {
        T /= 1-s[i].alpha;
        g[i]=T*(s[i].colour-suffix);
        suffix=s[i].alpha*s[i].colour+(1-s[i].alpha)*suffix;
    }
    return g;
}
```

# 675. A Stable Radix Sort Whose Empty Passes Still Move Every Payload

Use TypeScript 5.3.3 targeting ES2022 and Node.js 20.11.1 on one Intel Ice Lake server core. Keys are uint32 values and payloads are uint32 original record identifiers. This pass is the kernel of an already stable, four-pass, eight-bit LSD radix sort. The driver alternates distinct input/output key and payload buffers and zeroes `count` before each pass.

```typescript
function pass(keys: Uint32Array, vals: Uint32Array,
              outK: Uint32Array, outV: Uint32Array,
              count: Uint32Array, shift: number): void {
  count.fill(0);
  for (let i = 0; i < keys.length; ++i)
    ++count[(keys[i] >>> shift) & 255];
  let sum = 0;
  for (let b = 0; b < 256; ++b) {
    const n = count[b]; count[b] = sum; sum += n;
  }
  for (let i = 0; i < keys.length; ++i) {
    const k = keys[i], b = (k >>> shift) & 255;
    const p = count[b]++;
    outK[p] = k; outV[p] = vals[i];
  }
}
```

N is 0 through 2^26; keys, vals, outK and outV each have exactly N entries, count has 256 entries, and the baseline driver invokes shifts 0, 8, 16 and 24 in order. Payloads are opaque words and must move with keys. struct gap { uint16_t first, last; };
```c
void sack(struct item *a, unsigned count, uint32_t cumulative,
          const struct gap *gaps, unsigned ngaps) {
    for (unsigned i = 0; i < count; ++i) {
        int acked = a[i].tsn <= cumulative;
        for (unsigned j = 0; j < ngaps; ++j) {
```

~~~cpp
#include <cstdint>

std::array<uint32_t, 4> evaluate4(const uint32_t* c, std::size_t n,
                                 std::array<uint32_t, 4> x) {
    std::array<uint32_t, 4> y{};
    for (std::size_t k = n; k-- != 0;) {
~~~

# 684. Native Frame Reads and Java Cleanup

Use Java SE 21 and OpenJDK jdk-21+35 on Linux x86-64. In the first fixture there is one Java client thread, one Cleaner thread, and no explicit close during energy. The client need not retain another strong reference after invoking the method.
```java
import java.lang.ref.Cleaner;
import java.lang.ref.Reference;
import java.util.concurrent.atomic.AtomicLong;

final class NativeFrame implements AutoCloseable {
    static final Cleaner CLEANER = Cleaner.create();
    static final class State implements Runnable {
        final AtomicLong address;
        State(long p) { address = new AtomicLong(p); }
        public void run() {
            long p = address.getAndSet(0);
            if (p != 0) Native.free(p);
        }
    }
    final State state;
    final Cleaner.Cleanable cleanup;
    NativeFrame(long p) {
        state = new State(p);
        cleanup = CLEANER.register(this, state);
    }
    long energy() {
        long p = state.address.get();
        if (p == 0) throw new IllegalStateException("closed");
        return Native.energy(p);
    }
    public void close() { cleanup.clean(); }
}
// Native.allocate(), Native.energy(long), Native.free(long) follow the stated ABI.
```

```rust
struct Span { page: usize, off: usize, len: usize }
struct Packet { pages: Vec<Arc<Page>>, spans: Vec<Span> }

fn enqueue(frags: &[Fragment], tx: &TxQueue) {
    let mut p = Packet {
        pages: Vec::with_capacity(frags.len()),
        spans: Vec::with_capacity(frags.len()),
    };
    for f in frags {
        let new_page = p.pages.last().map_or(true,
            |last| !Arc::ptr_eq(last, &f.page));
        if new_page { p.pages.push(Arc::clone(&f.page)); }
        p.spans.push(Span { page: p.pages.len() - 1,
                            off: f.off, len: f.len });
    }
    tx.submit(p);
}
```

# 690. Radiance-Field Export across World Coordinate Scales

Use Python 3.12 and NumPy 2.1. A radiance field supplies density sigma in inverse metres and RGB colour in [0,1]. This is a discrete rendering contract, not a guarantee that a finite sample set equals a continuous volume integral.

A scene exporter applies X'=s R X+b, where s>0 changes the length unit, R is proper orthogonal and b is a translation. The exported ray uses o'=s R o+b, d'=s R d with unchanged t values. The intended exported field represents the same optical scene. One fixture has o=(0,0,0), d=(0,0,2), t=[0,1/4,1/2], constant density 1 and constant red colour 1 over both segments, against black. Export with s=3, R=I, b=(1,0,0). A second differentiable fixture uses sigma(x, y, z)=1+z²/16 and red colour 1/4+z/16 over z in [0,4], with the same sampling rule.

```python
import numpy as np

def render(o, d, t, field, background):
    T = 1.0
    C = np.zeros(3)
    for i in range(len(t)-1):
        x = o + t[i]*d
        sigma, colour = field(x)
        a = -np.expm1(-sigma*(t[i+1]-t[i]))
        C += T*a*colour
        T *= 1.0-a
    return C + T*background

def exported_field(xprime, scale, R, shift, old_field):
    x = R.T @ (xprime-shift) / scale
    sigma, colour = old_field(x)
    return sigma, colour
```

```cpp
void transpose64(unsigned long a[64]) {
    const unsigned long masks[6]={
        0x00000000ffffffffUL,0x0000ffff0000ffffUL,
        0x00ff00ff00ff00ffUL,0x0f0f0f0f0f0f0f0fUL,
        0x3333333333333333UL,0x5555555555555555UL};
    unsigned stage=0;
    for (unsigned s=32; s; s>>=1,++stage)
        for (unsigned base=0; base<64; base+=2*s)
            for (unsigned r=0; r<s; ++r) {
                unsigned i=base+r, j=i+s;
                unsigned long t=((a[i]>>s)^a[j])&masks[stage];
                a[i]^=t<<s;
                a[j]^=t;
            }
}
```

# 695. Dual-MAC Biquads with a Rounding Boundary between Every Stage

Use C++20, GCC 14.2, CMSIS-Core 6.0.0 and a little-endian Cortex-M7. Four independent channels each pass through six direct-form-I stages. Every coefficient and sample is signed16. A stage forms the exact sum `b0*x+b1*x1+b2*x2+a1*y1+a2*y2`, takes floor division by 32768, then clamps to [-32768,32767]. This rounded result feeds the next stage. Initial histories and coefficients are arbitrary signed16 values. This is the exact machine contract, without a real-number stability assumption.

```cpp
#include <bit>
#include <cstdint>
#include "cmsis_gcc.h" // CMSIS-Core6.0.0 intrinsic definitions
struct Hist { int16_t x1,x2,y1,y2; };
static uint32_t pair16(int16_t a, int16_t b) {
    return uint32_t(uint16_t(a)) | (uint32_t(uint16_t(b))<<16);
}
int16_t stage(int16_t x, Hist& h, const int16_t c[5]) {
    uint64_t z=uint64_t(int64_t(c[0])*x);
    z=__SMLALD(pair16(h.x1,h.x2),pair16(c[1],c[2]),z);
    z=__SMLALD(pair16(h.y1,h.y2),pair16(c[3],c[4]),z);
    int64_t s=std::bit_cast<int64_t>(z);
    int64_t q=s>=0 ? s/32768 : -((-s+32767)/32768);
    if (q>32767) q=32767;
    if (q< -32768) q= -32768;
    int16_t y=int16_t(q);
    h.x2=h.x1; h.x1=x; h.y2=h.y1; h.y1=y;
    return y;
}
```

No heap allocation or floating-point substitution is allowed.

```rust
use std::collections::BTreeMap;
struct SendRange {
    begin: u64,
    bytes: Vec<u8>,
    sent_on: Vec<(u8, u32, u32)>, // subflow, relative begin, length
}
struct Sender { retained: BTreeMap<u64, SendRange> }
impl Sender {
    fn data_ack(&mut self, next_dsn: u64) {
        self.retained.retain(|_, r|
            r.begin + r.bytes.len() as u64 > next_dsn);
    }
    fn subflow_timeout(&self, subflow: u8, relative: u32) -> Option<&[u8]> {
        self.retained.values().find_map(|r| {
            r.sent_on.iter().any(|&(s, first, len)|
                s == subflow && first <= relative && relative < first + len)
                .then_some(r.bytes.as_slice())
        })
    }
}
```

# 699. A UTF-16 Encoder with an ASCII Vector Path and a Precise Committed Prefix

Translation targets: AMD64 AVX2 and AArch64 NEON.

Use Java 17 char values, nonnull arrays, and no asynchronous exceptions. in.length<=1024 and out.length<=4096. Return bytes written on success, or -(i+1) for a malformed surrogate or insufficient output room at source index i. Every previously completed character remains encoded; the failing character writes nothing. The native adapter supplies UTF-16 code units and raw bytes; arrays are disjoint. Ordinary array exceptions are excluded by the shown checks.

```java
static int encode(char[] in,byte[] out) {
    int p=0;
    for(int i=0;i<in.length;i++) {
        int c=in[i], start=i;
        if(c>=0xd800 && c<=0xdbff) {
            if(i+1==in.length) return -(start+1);
            int d=in[i+1];
            if(d<0xdc00 || d>0xdfff) return -(start+1);
            c=0x10000+((c-0xd800)<<10)+(d-0xdc00); i++;
        } else if(c>=0xdc00 && c<=0xdfff) return -(start+1);
        int need=c<128?1:c<2048?2:c<65536?3:4;
        if(out.length-p<need) return -(start+1);
        if(need==1) out[p++]=(byte)c;
        else {
            for(int k=need-1;k>0;k--) out[p+k]=(byte)(0x80|((c>>(6*(need-1-k)))&63));
            out[p]=(byte)((need==2?0xc0:need==3?0xe0:0xf0)|(c>>(6*(need-1))));
            p+=need;
        }
    }
    return p;
}
```

A streaming decoder in TypeScript 5.4.5, emitted as ES2022 and run by Node.js 22.4.1 on an Arm Neoverse N2 core, already handles four ASCII bytes per iteration. The following fast path runs only in the accepting state. A caller falls back to the general machine at the returned input position.

```typescript
function asciiRun(src: Uint8Array, p: number, end: number,
                  dst: Uint32Array, k: number): [number, number] {
  while (p + 4 <= end && k + 4 <= dst.length) {
    const a = src[p], b = src[p+1], c = src[p+2], d = src[p+3];
    if (((a | b | c | d) & 0x80) !== 0) break;
    dst[k] = a; dst[k+1] = b; dst[k+2] = c; dst[k+3] = d;
    p += 4; k += 4;
  }
  while (p < end && k < dst.length && src[p] < 0x80)
    dst[k++] = src[p++];
  return [p, k];
}
```

The output buffer may fill after any scalar, and a resumed call receives more output capacity. UTF-8 must reject overlong encodings, surrogate encodings, scalars above U+10FFFF and stray continuation bytes. End-of-stream while nonaccepting is an error. Report the absolute offset of the earliest byte that makes the prefix impossible to extend to valid UTF-8; an incomplete but extendable final prefix instead reports the start offset of that incomplete sequence. Previously emitted scalars remain committed on error.

```typescript
function softmax(xs: number[]): number[] {
  const m = Math.max(...xs);
  const es = xs.map(x => Math.exp(x-m));
  const z = es.reduce((a,b) => a+b, 0);
  return es.map(x => x/z);
}
function confidence(S: number[][], va: boolean[], vb: boolean[]) {
  const rows = S.map(softmax);
  const cols = S[0].map((_,j) => softmax(S.map(r => r[j])));
  return S.map((r,i) => r.map((_,j) =>
    va[i] && vb[j] ? rows[i][j]*cols[j][i] : 0));
}
const transformedA = new Map<string, Float32Array>();
function featureKey(imageA: string, revisionA: number) {
  return `${imageA}:${revisionA}`;
}
```

~~~rust
fn range_basis(a: &Mat, omega: &Mat, power_steps: usize) -> Mat {
    let mut q = thin_qr(&mul(a, false, omega, false));
    for _ in 0..power_steps {
        let z = thin_qr(&mul(a, true, &q, false));
        q = thin_qr(&mul(a, false, &z, false));
    }
    q
}

fn probe_residual(a: &Mat, q: &Mat, probes: &Mat) -> Mat {
    let ag = mul(a, false, probes, false);
    let qt_ag = mul(q, true, &ag, false);

}
~~~

# 714. A Degeneracy-Oriented Triangle Counter with Reused Lists in the Wrong Order

The code below counts each triangle once using only forward-list intersections; uint64_t is large enough for all possible outputs at the stated n.

```cpp
std::uint64_t intersect(std::span<const std::uint32_t> a,
                        std::span<const std::uint32_t> b) {
    std::size_t i = 0, j = 0;
    std::uint64_t result = 0;
    while (i < a.size() && j < b.size()) {
        if (a[i] < b[j]) ++i;
        else if (b[j] < a[i]) ++j;
        else { ++result; ++i; ++j; }
    }
    return result;
}
std::uint64_t triangles(const CSR& g) {
    std::uint64_t total = 0;
    for (std::uint32_t u = 0; u < g.vertices(); ++u)
        for (auto v : g.forward(u))
            total += intersect(g.forward(u), g.forward(v));
    return total;
}
```

```typescript
type Frame = { fin: boolean; rsv1: boolean; opcode: number;

function frame(f: Frame) {
```

# 720. Authenticated Instructions Are Not Yet Published Instructions

A legitimate runtime decrypts a function immediately before first use. `open(record, aad, scratch)` is an authenticated-decryption oracle: it returns either the complete verified plaintext or failure, and no caller may use its output before success. use core::arch::x86_64::*;
```rust
#[target_feature(enable = "avx2")]
unsafe fn valid_utf8(b: &[u8]) -> bool {
    let mut i = 0usize;

}
```

```fortran
module bridge
  use iso_c_binding
  implicit none
  interface
    integer(c_int) function enqueue(p,n) bind(C)
      import c_ptr,c_int,c_size_t
      type(c_ptr), value :: p
      integer(c_size_t), value :: n

    real(c_double) function finish(ticket) bind(C)

contains
```

# 727. A Batched Ring Whose Metadata Is Cheap but Its Payload Still Migrates

Use C++20, GCC 14.2 and two pinned Neoverse N2 cores. A single producer and a single consumer exchange batches of exactly eight unsigned64 words through a 4,096-word ring. Counters never reach `2^60`; ring storage is ordinary coherent memory. Producer and consumer objects are private to their threads, and their cached positions start at zero. A successful producer call publishes all eight words; a successful consumer call returns the oldest eight. Calls may return false immediately when full or empty. Each x argument designates eight valid words outside the Ring object: initialized readable words for push8 and writable words for pop8. No other thread accesses that call buffer while the operation runs. No waiting, timeout or additional callback semantics are hidden.

```cpp
#include <atomic>
#include <cstdint>
struct alignas(128) Pos { std::atomic<uint64_t> v{0}; };
struct Ring { Pos read,write; alignas(64) uint64_t data[4096]; };
struct Producer {
    uint64_t w=0, cached_r=0;
    bool push8(Ring& q, const uint64_t* x) {
        if (w-cached_r+8>4096) {
            cached_r=q.read.v.load(std::memory_order_acquire);
            if (w-cached_r+8>4096) return false;
        }
        for (unsigned j=0;j<8;++j) q.data[(w+j)&4095]=x[j];
        w+=8; q.write.v.store(w,std::memory_order_release);
        return true;
    }
};
struct Consumer {
    uint64_t r=0, cached_w=0;
    bool pop8(Ring& q, uint64_t* x) {
        if (cached_w-r<8) {
            cached_w=q.write.v.load(std::memory_order_acquire);
            if (cached_w-r<8) return false;
        }
        for (unsigned j=0;j<8;++j) x[j]=q.data[(r+j)&4095];
        r+=8; q.read.v.store(r,std::memory_order_release);
        return true;
    }
};
```

You may use fixed per-block metadata, bounded credits or two-level rings, but total storage including metadata may not exceed48 KiB, and private state is limited to 256 bytes per thread. Every call must remain bounded and nonblocking in the operation-count sense; a false return may be conservative but successful operations must remain linearizable and preserve FIFO batches.

# 728. Multiview Depth Evidence and Metric Posterior Moments

Use Rust 1.85.0, edition 2024. A learned multiview stereo stage evaluates features on a reference-camera depth plane. Camera matrices are world-to-camera transforms X_i=R_i X_world+t_i with column vectors, and K_i maps positive-z camera coordinates to homogeneous pixel coordinates. To warp a reference pixel, backproject its depth in the reference camera, transform through world coordinates and then into each source camera, divide by positive z and bilinearly sample its feature map. A view is invalid at this plane/pixel when z<=0 or any required bilinear sample lies outside its valid image rectangle. Invalid observations are missing; they are not zero-valued feature measurements.

The plane cost is the mean squared deviation of valid feature vectors from their valid-view mean, including the reference view. A plane with fewer than two valid views is marked unavailable. All valid features are eight-dimensional vectors with entries in [-4,4]. There are at most five views, 64×48 reference pixels and 32 plane hypotheses. Every source feature grid is at most 64×48 cells; all stored feature scalars and camera/resize parameters are finite binary64 values with their represented values defining this numerical input. An external deterministic learned regularizer converts the cost volume and availability mask into a probability vector over available hypotheses; it is supplied for this task. Its probabilities sum to one exactly in the rational fixtures. The supplied regularizer adapter uses at most 8 MiB total private workspace and immutable parameter storage, accepts the resident cost/mask volume, and writes a caller-owned binary64 probability array; it retains no other input or output owners. At most one current and one previous completed result are live. Reconstructing or training this supplied bounded adapter is outside the task.

```rust
fn variance(warped: &[([f64; 8], bool)]) -> [f64; 8] {
    let mut sum = [0.0; 8];
    let mut sum2 = [0.0; 8];
    for (v, valid) in warped {
        for c in 0..8 {
            let x = if *valid { v[c] } else { 0.0 };
            sum[c] += x;
            sum2[c] += x*x;
        }
    }
    let n = warped.len() as f64;
    std::array::from_fn(|c| sum2[c]/n - (sum[c]/n).powi(2))
}
fn depth_from_inverse_planes(rho: &[f64], prob: &[f64]) -> f64 {
    let mean_rho: f64 = rho.iter().zip(prob).map(|(r,p)| r*p).sum();
    1.0/mean_rho
}
```

~~~rust
struct Wait {
    queue: std::rc::Rc<Queue>,
    link: Link,
    registered: bool,
    _pin: std::marker::PhantomPinned,
}

//   if not registered:

//       registered = true
//   return Pending

// Drop for Wait:
//   if registered:
//       queue.remove(pointer_to(link))
~~~

`register` stores the raw link pointer and may enqueue callbacks containing a copy. A callback can write that link and wake the task. # 737. A Tournament Merge That Minimizes Comparisons but Repeats Dependent Loads

Use TypeScript 5.3.3 targeting ES2022 and Node.js 20.11.1 on an AMD Zen 4 core. K sorted Uint32Array streams are merged by a tournament tree. K is a power of two from 2 through 256. `head[s]` caches the current key; exhausted streams have `live[s]=0`. Tree leaves store stream IDs, and ties are broken by smaller stream ID, preserving order within each input stream. The hot repair is already logarithmic and uses typed metadata.

```typescript
function better(a: number, b: number, live: Uint8Array,
                head: Uint32Array): number {
  if (live[a] === 0) return b;
  if (live[b] === 0) return a;
  const x = head[a], y = head[b];
  return x < y || (x === y && a < b) ? a : b;
}
function repair(tree: Uint16Array, live: Uint8Array,
                head: Uint32Array, k: number, s: number): void {
  let p = (k + s) >>> 1;
  while (p !== 0) {
    tree[p] = better(tree[2*p], tree[2*p+1], live, head);
    p >>>= 1;
  }
}
```

The surrounding driver emits `head[tree[1]]`, advances that stream, refreshes its cached head/live flag, and repairs the path. It stops after the known total N≤2^27 elements. Output is one supplied Uint32Array, and the required order is increasing `(key, stream_id, original_position)`, although only keys are stored. For validation, retain identities in a separate oracle. Extra production scratch beyond input/output is at most 64·K bytes. All tree building and output writes are timed.

# 739. A Linear-Time Gaussian Likelihood Whose Gradient Retains Quadratic State per Sample

Use CPython 3.12.7 and NumPy 2.1.3, with any native extension compiled by Clang 18.1.8. On an Intel Xeon Platinum 8480+, evaluate a zero-mean Gaussian log likelihood with K_ij=sum_{h=1}^r a_h rho_h^{|i-j|}+sigma2*1[i=j]. Here 1<=r<=16, 2^12<=n<=2^20, a_h and sigma2 are binary64 in [2^-20,1], rho_h is in [0,1-2^-20], and observations y_i lie in [-16,16]. Return the likelihood without its constant -n log(2pi)/2 and its derivatives with respect to log a_h, rho_h and log sigma2. The target matrix is the exact real formula on represented parameters.

The baseline already exploits semiseparable structure. The code computes the quadratic term and log determinant using r-dimensional state; u is sqrt(a), phi is rho, and the square-root rounding is part of the numerical analysis.

~~~python
import numpy as np

def structured_likelihood(y, a, rho, sigma2):
    u = np.sqrt(a)
    S = np.zeros((len(a), len(a)))
    f = np.zeros(len(a))
    old_w = np.zeros(len(a))
    old_d, old_z = 0.0, 0.0
    quad, logdet = 0.0, 0.0
    diag = sigma2 + a.sum()
    for value in y:
        S = rho[:, None] * (S + old_d*np.outer(old_w, old_w)) * rho[None, :]
        f = rho * (f + old_w*old_z)
        su = S @ u
        d = diag - u @ su
        w = (u - su) / d
        z = value - u @ f
        quad += z*z/d
        logdet += np.log(d)
        old_w, old_d, old_z = w, d, z
    return -0.5*(quad + logdet)
~~~

```ocaml
let lower_suffix text sa_at n pattern =
  let lo = ref (-1) and hi = ref n in
  let ll = ref 0 and lh = ref 0 in
  while !hi - !lo > 1 do
    let mid = !lo + (!hi - !lo) / 2 in
    let skip = min !ll !lh in
    let sign, matched = compare_from text (sa_at mid) pattern skip in
    if sign < 0 then begin lo := mid; ll := matched end
    else begin hi := mid; lh := matched end
  done;
```

# 748. Quantized Visual Descriptor Retrieval with Exact Ranking

For this question the instruction semantics are explicitly supplied: `_mm256_maddubs_epi16` forms adjacent unsigned-byte times signed-byte products and adds each pair with signed 16-bit saturation; `_mm256_madd_epi16` then multiplies pairs of signed 16-bit values and adds into signed 32-bit lanes.

```cpp
#include <immintrin.h>
#include <cstdint>
int dot32(const std::uint8_t* uq, const std::int8_t* d) {
    __m256i a = _mm256_loadu_si256((const __m256i*)uq);
    __m256i b = _mm256_loadu_si256((const __m256i*)d);
    __m256i pair = _mm256_maddubs_epi16(a,b);
    __m256i wide = _mm256_madd_epi16(pair,_mm256_set1_epi16(1));
    alignas(32) std::int32_t lane[8];
    _mm256_store_si256((__m256i*)lane,wide);
    int sum=0, correction=0;
    for (int x:lane) sum += x;
    for (int k=0;k<32;++k) correction += 128*int(d[k]);
    return sum-correction;
}
```

# 751. A Matrix Exponential Action Whose Safe Scaling Causes Hundreds of Sparse Passes

Use C++17 and Clang 18.1.8 on an EPYC 9654 socket. P is an n-by-n row-stochastic sparse matrix, n<=2^20, with at most 32 nonzeros per row. The baseline uses uniformization, splits theta so each stage has mean at most eight, and evaluates a Poisson-weighted sparse matrix-matrix polynomial. poisson_weights returns weights w_j=exp(-h)h^j/j! through a chosen m and an explicit upper bound on the omitted tail; its implementation and numerical error must be audited. axpy and spmm are already vectorized native kernels.

~~~cpp
Mat action(const CSR& P, const Mat& B, double theta, double eps) {
    const unsigned stages = std::max(1u, unsigned(std::ceil(theta / 8.0)));
    const double h = theta / stages;
    const auto w = poisson_weights(h, eps / (4.0*stages));
    Mat state = B, term(B.rows(), B.cols()), next(B.rows(), B.cols());
    for (unsigned s = 0; s < stages; ++s) {
        term = state;
        next = scaled(term, w.values[0]);
        for (std::size_t j = 1; j < w.values.size(); ++j) {
            term = spmm(P, term);
            axpy(next, w.values[j], term);
        }
        state.swap(next);
    }
    return state;
}
~~~

# 755. Concurrent ESP Authentication and Replay Windows

Use ISO C11 with GCC 13.3.0 and an offline ESP receiver under RFC 4303. There is one single-sender unicast Security Association with integrity protection and a 64-packet anti-replay window. A supplied cryptographic primitive authenticates the exact immutable ESP bytes, including the sequence information required by the negotiated transform, and writes candidate plaintext into private staging storage. It returns success or failure synchronously to a worker but workers finish in arbitrary order. No plaintext is visible until the replay-commit step also accepts the packet.

The following shared state uses sequentially consistent atomics, so the model has no C data race on top or bits. Bit zero denotes the current highest accepted full sequence; higher bits describe earlier sequences. For this kernel, candidate has already been reconstructed as a full sequence number and is at least top in the shown schedules.

```c
struct replay { _Atomic uint64_t top, bits; };
int receive(struct replay *r, uint64_t candidate, struct packet *p) {
    uint64_t old = atomic_load(&r->top);
    uint64_t mask = atomic_load(&r->bits);
    if (candidate == old && (mask & 1)) return 0;
    if (candidate < old) return 0; /* simplified preliminary filter */
    if (!authenticate_private(p, candidate)) return 0;
    uint64_t shift = candidate - old;
    uint64_t next = shift >= 64 ? 1 : ((mask << shift) | 1);
    atomic_store(&r->top, candidate);
    atomic_store(&r->bits, next);
    publish_plaintext(p);
    return 1;
}
```

Initially top is 100 and bits is 1. Worker A handles sequence 101 and worker B handles sequence 103. Both pass the preliminary stage and authenticate successfully; B commits before A. A third arrival replays the exact authenticated sequence-103 packet. Give the complete top/bitmap/output history. In a separate schedule, two workers authenticate duplicate sequence 101 against the same initial snapshot. Explain why making each scalar atomic, or placing an acquire fence before publication, does not by itself make replay admission indivisible.

A preliminary check may avoid expensive work, but only authenticated data may advance the replay window. The final check must use the current committed window and atomically claim a previously unaccepted sequence before releasing its plaintext. One mutex around this final state transition is allowed; authentication stays outside it. A packet initially admissible may become too old while it is being authenticated. Specify the resulting disposition without relabeling its authenticated sequence number.

Add an ESN fixture beginning at full top `0x00000007fffffffe`: receive low wire sequence 1, then a delayed low sequence `fffffffd`. Use the RFC Appendix A window-based reconstruction, with a maximum sequence gap of 512 and no 64-bit wrap. The high word chosen for cryptographic verification must remain associated with that verification result; recomputing a different candidate after authentication would require separate verification. Include an unauthenticated far-future packet and show that it cannot move the committed window.

There are four worker slots, packet payloads of at most 1024 bytes, two SA storage slots, and at most eight SA generations, which do not wrap. Use diagnostic sequence/SA tokens instead of key material. # 756. A Balanced Aggregate Merge Tree That Repeatedly Copies the Large Run

Use Haskell2010 with BangPatterns, GHC 8.10.7 at -O2, vector 0.12.3.1, Linux 6.12, and an x86-64 out-of-order server. Input consists of p≤2^16 immutable unboxed vectors of sorted, distinct (Word32,Word64) pairs. Each vector is a page-local aggregate; total input pairs N≤2^26. The result contains every key appearing in any input, in ascending order, with values added modulo 2^64. A zero accumulated value does not remove a key. All input vectors are fully evaluated before the operation.

```haskell
{-# LANGUAGE BangPatterns #-}
import Data.Word
import qualified Data.Vector.Unboxed as U

type Run = U.Vector (Word32, Word64)

-- merge is a conventional linear two-cursor merge: equal keys
-- are combined with Word64 addition, otherwise the smaller pair
-- is copied. It allocates one output buffer and preserves keys.
reduce :: (Run -> Run -> Run) -> [Run] -> Run
reduce merge = finish
  where
    finish []  = U.empty
    finish [a] = a
    finish xs  = finish (rounds xs)
    rounds (a:b:rest) = let !c = merge a b
                        in c : rounds rest
    rounds rest = rest
```

The baseline is a balanced reduction tree over already compressed page aggregates, not a left fold inserting raw records into a map. Your policy must charge any sampled or exact overlap discovery and any sorting/bucketing of run descriptors. The result must be independent of merge order because the specified modular operation is associative; no floating-point reassociation is allowed.

Parallel execution on at most sixteen workers is permitted, but its queueing and temporary results must fit the same cap.

# 759. A Flat Combiner That Saves Counter Atomics but Polls Every Cold Slot

Use Rust 1.85.0, edition 2021, opt-level=3 on Linux 6.12. Compare a two-socket x86-64 server with an AArch64 server build. There are 64 producers and 4096 counters. Each producer owns a cache-line-aligned request slot and has at most one outstanding request. It stores a valid key and delta with Relaxed, then state=1 with Release. It waits for state=2 with Acquire, reads the result, and only then reuses its slot. A mutex permits exactly one combiner to hold the mutable counter array at a time. No cancellations or producer exits occur.

```rust
fn combine(slots: &[Slot], counters: &mut [u64]) -> usize {
    let mut done = 0;
    for s in slots {
        if s.state.load(Ordering::Acquire) != 1 { continue; }
        let key = s.key.load(Ordering::Relaxed) as usize;
        let delta = s.delta.load(Ordering::Relaxed);
        let answer = counters[key].wrapping_add(delta);
        counters[key] = answer;
        s.result.store(answer, Ordering::Relaxed);
        s.state.store(2, Ordering::Release);
        done += 1;
    }
    done
}
```

Slot's key, delta, result, and state are atomic fields; alignment/padding prevents two slots sharing a cache line. The result of add_and_get is the new counter value at a legal linearization point, with arithmetic modulo 2^64. The baseline amortizes one mutex acquisition over a batch and updates counters without per-operation RMW instructions. If requests are grouped by key, each returned prefix value must correspond to that order, rather than giving every producer the final batch total. Cross-shard operations are absent, so state exactly which independence your design exploits.

The shared request/dispatch metadata is capped at 128 KiB, excluding the fixed slots and counters. Each producer must make progress under an explicit fair scheduling assumption; no lock-free or bounded-wall-time claim follows merely from using atomics. # 761. Thenable Admission into a Two-Slot Image Broker

Use TypeScript 5.7.3 targeting ES2024 and ECMAScript 2024 Promise semantics. A single-thread image broker owns two fixed four-byte slots. Admission may receive an untrusted thenable from a decoder plugin. The plugin is ordinary JavaScript: retrieving its `then` property may run a getter, and the returned method may later fulfill or reject. It may invoke broker.close from that getter. There are no proxies, workers, SharedArrayBuffers, or native threads.

close must prevent any tile commit from beginning after it returns, release every reserved slot exactly once once no commit can use it, and make outstanding admissions reject as closed. Already enqueued ECMAScript jobs may still run; the contract concerns broker commits and ownership rather than suppressing arbitrary plugin code. Each thenable has at most one getter, one then-method invocation, and at most two calls to its supplied resolving functions. Zero calls are permitted, including a then-method that returns without settling. Promise first-settlement rules apply. The source is not assumed to be a native Promise. Intrinsics and prototypes are unmodified; fulfillment values are plain accessor-free Uint8Array objects from the same realm. Plugin code may invoke close and its resolving functions, but cannot directly edit broker fields or call submit recursively.

```typescript
type Ticket = { slot: number; cancelled: boolean };
class Broker {
  closed = false;
  free = [0, 1];
  active = new Map<number, Ticket>();
  slots = [new Uint8Array(4), new Uint8Array(4)];
  submit(input: unknown): Promise<number> {
    if (this.closed || this.free.length === 0)
      return Promise.reject(new Error("closed or full"));
    const slot = this.free.pop()!;
    const ready = Promise.resolve(input);
    const ticket = { slot, cancelled: false };
    this.active.set(slot, ticket);
    return ready.then(value => {
      if (ticket.cancelled) throw new Error("closed");
      if (!(value instanceof Uint8Array) || value.length !== 4)
        throw new Error("format");
      this.slots[slot].set(value);
      return slot;
    }).finally(() => {
      this.active.delete(slot);
      this.free.push(slot);
    });
  }
  close(): void {
    this.closed = true;
    for (const t of this.active.values()) t.cancelled = true;
  }
}
```

No user getter, plugin method, or external callback may execute while the broker's bookkeeping is half-published. Closed submissions must never be resurrected by a later settlement. close must itself reject and retire outstanding admissions without waiting for plugin settlement; a never-settling thenable cannot retain a slot after close returns.

The oracle may model only these specified thenables and ordinary Promise resolution, but it must preserve the relevant job ordering. # 783. Compiling a Transactional RAII Loop through Its Exceptional Exits

Translation targets: AMD64 System V and AArch64.

Use C++20, the Itanium C++ exception ABI, and ordinary Linux user-space DWARF unwinding. Exclude asynchronous cancellation, signals that throw, and resource exhaustion in the stipulated helpers. reserve is nonthrowing and returns a unique opaque token; cancel and publish are noexcept and each consumes that token exactly once. transform may throw a typed Fault at a selected index before returning. It has no other externally visible effect. tmp and src are disjoint arrays of n uint32, n<=64. publish atomically copies all n tmp words into a separate destination; cancel publishes nothing.

```cpp
struct Guard {
    Token t;
    bool done=false;
    ~Guard() noexcept { if(!done) cancel(t); }
};
void update(const uint32_t *src,uint32_t *tmp,size_t n) {
    Guard g{reserve()};
    for(size_t i=0;i<n;++i) tmp[i]=transform(src[i],i);
    publish(g.t,tmp,n);
    g.done=true;
}
```

Helper bodies remain external under the stated contracts; token is one pointer-sized word. ```python

```python
    return ("add", full - (1 << 32), ell - 1)
```

```haskell
      End -> End
      Skip t -> Skip t
      Emit x t -> Emit (f x) t

filterS p (Stream next s0) = Stream step s0
  where
    step s = case next s of
      End -> End
      Skip t -> Skip t
      Emit x t -> if p x then Emit x t else Skip t

sumS (Stream next s0) = go s0 0
  where
    go !s !a = case next s of
      End -> a
      Skip t -> go t a
      Emit x t -> go t (a+x)
```

# 819. A Certified Quadrature Batch Whose Hardest Peak Dictates Every SIMD Lane

Use CPython 3.12.7, NumPy 2.1.3 and a native kernel compiled by Clang 18.1.8. Compare Intel Xeon Platinum 8480+ and Graviton3. A batch contains 1 through 64 integrals I(a,c)=integral_0^1 a/[a+(x-c)^2] dx. Parameters are exact dyadics: a=2^(-2k), 0<=k<=8, and c=j/4096, 0<=j<=4096. Return a dyadic enclosing interval of width at most 2^-b for each integral, 10<=b<=30.
~~~python
import numpy as np

def batched_simpson(a, centres, panels=2**17, block=4096):
    result = np.zeros(len(a), dtype=np.float64)
    for lo in range(0, panels + 1, block):
        ix = np.arange(lo, min(lo + block, panels + 1), dtype=np.int64)
        x = ix.astype(np.float64) / panels
        weights = np.where(ix & 1, 4.0, 2.0)
        weights[(ix == 0) | (ix == panels)] = 1.0
        delta = x[:, None] - centres[None, :]
        values = a[None, :] / (a[None, :] + delta*delta)
        result += weights @ values
    return result / (3.0*panels)
~~~

# 822. A Multiway Join Whose Worst-Case Certificate Survives Its Fast Iterator

```cpp
void visit(unsigned depth, Tuple& prefix, const Query& q,
           const Indexes& index, Sink& sink) {
    if (depth == q.variables()) { sink.emit(prefix); return; }
    auto sets = index.extensions(q, depth, prefix);
    auto driver = std::min_element(sets.begin(), sets.end(),
        [](const auto& x, const auto& y) { return x.size() < y.size(); });
    for (std::uint32_t x : *driver) {
        bool present = true;
        for (auto s : sets)
            if (!std::binary_search(s.begin(), s.end(), x)) {
                present = false; break;
            }
        if (present) { prefix[depth] = x;
                       visit(depth + 1, prefix, q, index, sink); }
    }
}
```

# 823. Expected Pose Loss over a Finite Hypothesis Set

Use Python 3.12 for an independent arithmetic reference and C++20 for an optional batched implementation. A localization network predicts horizontal scene coordinates X_i(w)=a_i+sum_j B_ij w_j from eight trainable scalars w. It estimates only horizontal camera translation h. Reprojection is f(X_i-h)/Z_i. The true translation h_star is a dyadic multiple of 1/64 in [-2,2].

Sixteen ordered two-observation subsets are supplied and fixed. A hypothesis h_k minimizes the two weighted squared pixel residuals with unit weights, so it is a rational differentiable function of w and has a positive denominator bounded away from zero. Its score is s_k=-sum_i r_ki²/(1+r_ki²), where r_ki=(f(X_i-h_k)/Z_i-u_i)/64. Define p_k=exp(s_k)/sum_l exp(s_l), L_k=(h_k-h_star)², and the objective F=sum_k p_k L_k. All hypotheses remain present; neither hard inlier pruning nor changing the subset list is part of this function.

```python
import math

def expected_loss(hypotheses, scores, truth):
    m = max(scores)
    e = [math.exp(s-m) for s in scores]
    z = sum(e)
    p = [x/z for x in e]
    L = [(h-truth)**2 for h in hypotheses]
    return sum(a*b for a,b in zip(p,L)), p

def proposed_gradient(hypotheses, dh_dw, scores, truth):
    F, p = expected_loss(hypotheses, scores, truth)
    g = [0.0]*8
    for k,h in enumerate(hypotheses):
        for j in range(8):
            g[j] += p[k]*2*(h-truth)*dh_dw[k][j]
    return F, g
```

# 829. HTTP/2 Scheduling across Window Changes and Stream Reset

Construct a bounded HTTP/2 sender in Rust 1.85.1 and an independent Python 3.12 verifier. RFC 9113 supplies the wire rules; the following local scheduling and completion model is additional. One owner serializes connection events, while two producer threads submit immutable application buffers through a queue. Transport submission either fails before accepting any bytes or accepts a complete immutable frame. Accepted frames reach the peer in submission order. A later completion releases their buffers; it does not return HTTP/2 credit. The peer may reset streams or change SETTINGS while accepted frames remain retained locally.

Here is an executable kernel after ordinary type definitions. `wire_payload` includes a Pad Length octet when PADDED is set and the padding itself; `application.len()` excludes both. `spent` is a local per-stream accumulator.

```rust
fn send_data(c: &mut Connection, id: u32, f: Frame) -> bool {
    let s = c.streams.get_mut(&id).unwrap();
    let n = f.application.len() as i64;
    if c.window < n || s.window < n { return false; }
    c.window -= n;
    s.window -= n;
    s.spent += n;
    c.transport.accept(f); // stipulated success in this kernel
    true
}
fn reset(c: &mut Connection, id: u32) {
    let s = c.streams.remove(&id).unwrap();
    c.window += s.spent;
}
fn new_initial_window(c: &mut Connection, value: u32) {
    for s in c.streams.values_mut() { s.window = value as i64; }
    c.initial_window = value;
}
```

Start from a legal connection state reached through earlier traffic: connection send credit is 8, SETTINGS_INITIAL_WINDOW_SIZE is 6, and streams 1 and 3 each have send credit 6. Stream 1 submits DATA containing `ABC`, a Pad Length value 2, and two padding octets. The peer then advertises initial stream window 2 and sends RST_STREAM for stream 1. Next it sends a connection WINDOW_UPDATE increment 4, and stream 3 requests unpadded DATA `xy`. Derive credit and ownership after every event, including the period when stream 1's previously submitted DATA backing allocation is still retained by transport. Supply a variant in which the first DATA submission fails, and one in which only an unsent reservation existed at reset.

The implementation must handle four active streams, 32 external events, eight outstanding frame owners, application fragments of 1–8 bytes, and padding of 0–3 bytes. The 9-byte frame header is outside flow-control debit. Accept syntactically valid WINDOW_UPDATE and SETTINGS values up to their RFC limits using wide checked intermediates; malformed increments and overflow have explicit connection/stream error dispositions. A stream window can be negative after a SETTINGS reduction. Keep peer-granted credit, temporary local reservations, submitted bytes, and retained allocation bytes distinguishable. A reset does not turn previously transmitted DATA into unused connection credit.

Specify a work-conserving round-robin policy: whenever an eligible queued frame fits both windows and transport has a free owner slot, the next owner step must submit one. Splitting application data into smaller frames is allowed only at documented byte boundaries and must account for the selected padding of each emitted frame. Rejection of all work and unlimited copying do not meet the contract. Total retained application/frame storage is limited to 16 KiB, including bases, queue nodes, and metadata; document the allocator accounting convention.

Deliver the sender, incremental frame parser, event log, and a refinement relation to a mathematical credit ledger. Produce a machine-checkable local transition certificate for a reduced one-stream model with connection credit 0–6, stream credit −3–6, and each queue/reservation/retention counter 0–3; enumerate guards and boundary transitions without enumerating arbitrary network histories. The verifier must reject undercharging padding, resetting windows to an absolute value, credit refunds on transmitted reset data, and early owner reclamation. Explain how the invariant extends to the four-stream bound. Include optimized artifact inspection locating signed comparisons and checked additions, and replay actual counterexample events against the compiled sender. The certificate and checker together must fit 2 MiB; this is a bounded refinement obligation, not a claim about all HTTP/2 implementations.

# 830. An Optimal Periodic Schedule for Four Nonlinear Integer Streams

```asm

.Lround:
    mov  rax,[rdi]
    xor  r8,rax
    ror  r8,13
    imul r8,r8,0x1e35a7bd
    mov  rax,[rdi+8]
    xor  r9,rax
    ror  r9,13
    imul r9,r9,0x1e35a7bd

    xor  r11,rax
```

# 833. A Reentrant Trace Protocol for a Fixed Pool

Use C11 on one thread. A fixed pool contains three 16-byte blocks with integer identities 0, 1, 2 and sentinel 3. All allocator operations and trace hooks are ordinary synchronous C calls; this is not an ISO C signal-handler model. A hook may query the pool and perform up to two allocator operations on its own handles before returning. Nesting is limited to two hook levels below the outer call. Each operation, including allocation failure, produces exactly one trace event. Eight outer client operations therefore generate at most 56 total operations.

The observable contract includes unique block ownership, correct allocation failure when all three blocks are live, and an event stream consistent with the linearization of each operation. A hook must always see a valid free/live partition. Owner identifiers are 1, 2, and 3. Clients release only currently owned handles; the allocator must not manufacture two simultaneously valid handles for the same block. Trace storage is fixed, with 64 event slots and bounded recursion metadata. All hooks terminate, never longjmp, and use no external allocator. The example omits payload bytes but not the disputed control sequence.

```c
#include <stdint.h>
#include <stdlib.h>
enum { NONE = 3 };
static uint8_t head = 0, next[3] = {1,2,NONE}, owner[3] = {0,0,0};
extern void emit(unsigned kind, unsigned block, unsigned who);

int acquire(unsigned who) {
    unsigned id = head;
    if (id == NONE) { emit(2, NONE, who); return -1; }
    emit(0, id, who);
    head = next[id];
    owner[id] = (uint8_t)who;
    return (int)id;
}
void release(unsigned id, unsigned who) {
    if (id >= 3 || owner[id] != who) abort();
    emit(1, id, who);
    owner[id] = 0;
    next[id] = head;
    head = (uint8_t)id;
}
// emit first appends a primitive-value event, then may invoke the bounded hook.
// Hook owners are distinct from the outer owner and from each active parent hook.
```

Then construct a repaired allocator and tracing layer that meets the contract for every permitted hook tree. The hook's observation must correspond to an already completed ownership transition; disabling all hooks or dropping events is not a repair. At most 512 bytes of explicit trace and allocator metadata are available in addition to the 48 payload bytes. Include all pending event records, depth counters, owners, and freelist entries in that accounting.

Emit an independently checkable certificate for the repaired C state machine. The checker may accept a restricted grammar of straight-line assignments, bounds checks, and calls to the explicit hook boundary; it must reject unrecognized operations. Its trusted semantics must include the callback stack and the order of state publication relative to event append. The certificate can use local invariants and induction over the three possible invocation depths, avoiding enumeration of every complete 56-event history. Define a concrete finite summary relation at each depth and show that checking its transitions is feasible within a stated resource bound.

The verification must establish unique live ownership, acyclic complete freelist coverage, no access through an invalid block index, exact event count, and correspondence between an event and the pool state visible when the hook begins. Include failed allocation, immediate hook allocation and release, two nested acquisitions, and a hook observing a nearly empty pool. Do not strengthen client premises so that all interesting reentry disappears. Payload reads and writes are allowed only through a currently owned handle and are otherwise abstracted by three small byte arrays.

Build a second reference implementation that uses an explicit free-set and owner map instead of the linked freelist. Differentially exercise all pool ownership states and bounded hook summaries, and have the independent checker reject certificates that move event emission one statement earlier or omit a freelist update. If using generated C, bind the certificate to its normalized source and the executable hash; separately inspect actual disassembly around every hook call to ensure the analyzed publication boundary is the one compiled.

For debugging, explain why an allocator-backed logging library would violate the stipulated hook model unless its reentry is included, and why removing the trace can remove the bug entirely. Hardware watchpoints and a fixed event buffer can expose the transition without adding an unmodeled callback. Deliver C code, summary certificates, independent checker, exact memory bounds, and observed or explicitly unavailable compiler evidence. The result certifies this small reentrant allocator and its instrumentation, not arbitrary C allocators or arbitrary signal interruption.

This is the central stable boundary search; A precedes B in the original run order, so equality belongs to A first.

```cpp
__device__ int corank(int d, const uint64_t* A, int na,
                      const uint64_t* B, int nb) {
  int lo=max(0,d-nb), hi=min(d,na);
  while (lo<hi) {
    int i=lo+(hi-lo)/2, j=d-i;
    if (j>0 && i<na && B[j-1]>=A[i]) lo=i+1;
    else hi=i;

  return lo;
}
// At diagonal d: take corank(d,...) entries from A and d-that from B.
```

```rust
#[derive(Clone, Copy)]
struct Box3 { lo: [i64;3], hi: [i64;3] }
fn centre(b: Box3) -> [i64;3] {
    std::array::from_fn(|k| (b.lo[k]+b.hi[k]).div_euclid(2))
}
fn score(r: Mat3i, t: [i64;3], pairs: &[Pair]) -> i64 {
    pairs.iter().map(|p| {

}

}
```

# 844. An Optimal Replay Schedule That Still Retains Too Many Checkpoints

Use GHC 9.6.6 and vector 0.13.1.0 on an Intel Ice Lake server core. A pure recurrence produces immutable vectors x_0 through x_T. The consumer needs x_(T−1), …, x_0 in exactly that reverse order.
```haskell
{-# LANGUAGE BangPatterns #-}
walk step visit lo hi slots x !acc
  | lo == hi = acc
  | hi-lo == 1 = visit lo x acc
  | slots == 0 = replay (hi-1) acc
  | otherwise =
      let mid = lo + (hi-lo) `quot` 2
          !xm = advance lo mid x
          !a1 = walk step visit mid hi (slots-1) xm acc
      in walk step visit lo mid slots x a1
  where
    advance !l !h !s
      | l == h = s
      | otherwise = advance (l+1) h (step l s)
    replay !j !a
      | j < lo = a
      | otherwise =
          let !s = advance lo j x

          in replay (j-1) a1
```

# 851. Certifying a Rust Decoder for Bounded Tile Records

Use Rust 1.85.0, edition 2021, on Linux x86-64 with eight-bit bytes. A camera packet has one through four 12-byte record headers followed by immutable payload bytes; the whole packet is at most 128 bytes. A separate trusted framing layer supplies the number of headers but does not validate their contents. The enabled byte must be exactly 0 or 1. Each header’s wire positions are fixed: enabled at 0, reserved zero bytes 1..3, offset as little-endian u32 at 4, count as little-endian u16 at 8, kind at 10, and reserved zero byte 11. Kind 1 means raw signed 16 samples and kind 3 means signed 16 deltas accumulated in mathematical signed 32 arithmetic.

An enabled header has count 1..8 and an even offset at or beyond the end of all headers. Its payload interval must be in bounds. Disabled headers require count 0, offset 0, and kind 1. Enabled payload intervals must be disjoint and together exactly cover the packet suffix. The required decoder returns all logical sample sequences or the first error offset under this order: reject truncated headers at input length; check all header fields in increasing wire-byte order; then check each enabled interval for even offset, header exclusion, and bounds in header order, reporting its offset-field byte. Finally sort intervals by start and header index and require consecutive coverage of the suffix, reporting the first disagreeing interval’s offset-field byte or input length for trailing uncovered bytes. Disabled offset/count checks occur at their own field bytes. Failure leaves caller output unchanged. The sketch incorrectly treats wire validity as something to inspect after forming a native Rust value.

```rust
#[repr(u8)]
#[derive(Clone, Copy)]
enum Kind { Raw = 1, Delta = 3 }
#[repr(C)]
#[derive(Clone, Copy)]
struct Header { enabled: bool, offset: u32, count: u16, kind: Kind }

unsafe fn header(bytes: &[u8]) -> Result<Header, usize> {
    if bytes.len() < 12 { return Err(bytes.len()); }
    let h = bytes.as_ptr().cast::<Header>().read_unaligned();
    if h.enabled && h.count > 8 { return Err(8); }
    if !matches!(h.kind, Kind::Raw | Kind::Delta) { return Err(10); }
    Ok(h)
}
fn sample(raw: &[u8], p: usize) -> i32 {
    i16::from_le_bytes([raw[p], raw[p+1]]) as i32
}
// The original caller casts each header, then checks offsets and decodes its payload.
```

First identify every validity, representation, and framing obligation that this sketch checks too late or not at all. Supply a concrete twelve-byte invalid-value witness and a separate valid-value but invalid-interval witness. Do not assign a mandated panic or branch outcome once an invalid bool or enum has been produced. Explain why read_unaligned addresses alignment but not type validity, and why repr(C) does not define this canonical wire format or authorize interpreting reserved bytes as native padding.

Construct a safe, allocation-free parser generator for this fixed format and record counts 1..4. Its generated Rust may use integer loads from byte arrays, checked indexing, and explicit field constructors after validation; it may not transmute arbitrary bytes into bool, enum, reference, or NonZero types. Runtime working storage is at most 256 bytes beyond immutable input and caller output. A private staged 32-element i32 result is permitted. Specify output lengths and commit order, including exact signed delta bounds and preservation of untouched caller slots.

Each generated parser must carry a certificate describing byte ranges, field predicates, dependency order, payload interval proofs, and every error exit. Build an independent checker for a small declared parser-plan language: scalar byte/u16/u32 reads, comparisons, bounded header loops, interval checks, raw/delta loops, and final commit. The checker must reconstruct its obligations from the generated plan, reject unsupported operations, and bind the accepted plan to normalized generated Rust. It may use compositional integer and finite-domain proofs; exhaustive enumeration of all 128-byte packets is not required. State the compiler/runtime trust boundary separately from the plan proof.

Provide a separate Python decoder with direct byte semantics and a finite corpus exhausting one-header field boundary classes, all record counts, disabled records, overlapping or gapped intervals, reserved bytes, malformed discriminants, truncated inputs, and extreme signed samples. Mutate a certificate to skip each required predicate or reorder an error check, and demonstrate rejection. Tests are corroboration; the certificate must establish the full bounded-format guarantee.

For diagnostics, inspect MIR or native output when the target compiler exists and run Miri only on the safe repaired parser or a clearly isolated invalid-input experiment. Explain how compiler assumptions about valid enum values can remove a post-construction check and why a debugger displaying an invalid discriminant does not make the operation legitimate. Deliver generator, parser, independent checker, certificates, byte-level oracle, and exact storage accounting.

# 852. Exact Poisson-Binomial Tails after the Polynomial Has Been Packed into an Integer

Use C++14, Clang 18.1.8 and GMP 6.3.0 on EPYC 9654 and Intel Xeon Platinum 8480+. Independent Bernoulli variables have probabilities a_i/256, with 0<=a_i<=256 and 1<=n<=4096. Return all exact integer coefficients of F(z)=product_i [(256-a_i)+a_i z], plus every cumulative tail sum requested by an increasing index list. Probabilities are these integers divided by 256^n. Underflow, tiny tails and deterministic variables are part of the domain; approximate floating coefficients are not acceptable outputs.

A balanced product tree already replaces scalar coefficient convolution with packed big-integer multiplication. A node representing s Bernoulli factors has nonnegative coefficients summing to 256^s. The merge packs both children at the parent's common base and extracts the product; the surrounding tree releases child storage after a merge.

~~~cpp
#include <gmpxx.h>
#include <vector>

std::vector<mpz_class> packed_merge(const std::vector<mpz_class>& a,
                                  const std::vector<mpz_class>& b,
                                  unsigned parent_factors) {
    const mp_bitcnt_t bits = 8*parent_factors + 1;
    mpz_class aa = 0, bb = 0;
    for (std::size_t i = a.size(); i-- != 0;) { aa <<= bits; aa += a[i]; }
    for (std::size_t i = b.size(); i-- != 0;) { bb <<= bits; bb += b[i]; }
    mpz_class product = aa * bb;
    const mpz_class mask = (mpz_class(1) << bits) - 1;
    std::vector<mpz_class> c(a.size() + b.size() - 1);
    for (auto& x : c) { x = product & mask; product >>= bits; }
    return c;
}
~~~

Construct two exact engines: an improved packed-integer tree and a modular-transform tree with Chinese remaindering. Audit the claim that the existing asymptotically fast integer multiplication makes its surrounding packing optimal. Count repeated shifts, allocation, coefficient extraction, tree imbalance caused by deterministic factors and final tail production. For the modular route, derive a node-specific bound on coefficients, choose enough pairwise coprime primes, validate roots of unity, prove every lazy-reduction range and reconstruct canonical nonnegative coefficients uniquely. Prime/root preparation and CRT work are charged; a fixed small set of convenient primes cannot represent arbitrarily large exact coefficients here.

Supply a dispatcher and an independently written Python 3.12 verifier. The certificate must establish every product-tree merge, the complete root coefficient vector, sum F(1)=256^n and all requested tails. A verifier using exact packed-integer identities and carry bounds is allowed; a few random evaluation points are only a diagnostic, not a deterministic certificate. Generic GMP/MPFR integer primitives are permitted, but neither an existing probability-distribution library nor an existing multiprime polynomial engine may replace the central implementation. The verifier must reject a coefficient reduced modulo an insufficient CRT product and an off-by-one tail boundary.

Prove bit-operation, memory and certificate bounds over n<=4096. Peak producer scratch including retained tree nodes, transforms and reconstruction is at most 512 MiB, excluding final coefficients; stream primes or levels where necessary. Compare fully parallel prime transforms with lower-memory streaming and explain how NUMA placement and integer-size thresholds change the crossover. Your optimality claim is confined to the two engine families, allowed node thresholds and a documented primitive-cost model, with separate empirical validation.

Inspect GMP's actually dispatched multiplication routines, allocation traces and the final NTT butterfly assembly. Determine whether time is spent in limb multiplication, repacking, modular reduction or CRT reconstruction. Include all a_i=128, many a_i in {0,256}, extreme tails and a single cold call. Provide exact small exhaustive fixtures and at least one full-bound resource witness. Hardware unavailable for timing permits conditional results, but exact outputs, independent verification and the asymptotic/bit-cost arguments remain required.

# 855. A Callback-Aware Typed-Array JIT That Resumes after the Last Commit

Translation targets: AMD64 AVX2 and AArch64.

Use TypeScript 5.9.3/ECMAScript 2024. xs and out are attached fixed-length Int32Array views of the same length n<=256. Their buffers may alias with arbitrary element displacement. beforeBlock is synchronous and may mutate array contents or throw, but cannot detach/resize buffers or introduce workers. It is called exactly once before each block of 16 logical elements. The runtime may move wrapper objects but pins the raw backing stores for the duration of a native block.

```typescript
function run(xs:Int32Array,out:Int32Array,beforeBlock:(b:number)=>void){
    for(let base=0;base<xs.length;base+=16){
        beforeBlock(base);
        const end=Math.min(base+16,xs.length);
        for(let i=base;i<end;++i)
            out[i]=(Math.imul(xs[i],17)+(out[i]>>>3))|0;
    }
}
```

SIMD is required for disjoint ranges and exactly identical views; partial overlaps must retain the sequential dependencies of the source. A failed fast-path guard after a callback must resume that same block rather than replaying its callback. Derive a state record identifying committed prefix, next callback, live roots and current block, and relate each native PC range to that record.

The permitted optimization domain is the stated guarded model, not arbitrary JavaScript objects or asynchronous callback interleavings.

# 856. A Direction-Switching BFS That Must Pay for Every Abandoned Probe

Use Rust 1.85.0, edition 2021, opt-level=3 on Linux 6.12 and an x86-64 many-core server. The graph is a validated immutable undirected simple CSR with n≤2^26 vertices and m≤2^30 edges. Construction is reported separately; a query begins with that representation available. A BFS must return exact distances from one source and may choose any legal parent. Neighbor order is adversarial. An existing hybrid avoids push work during dense frontiers, but chooses direction using a heuristic:

```rust
fn level(g: &Graph, frontier: &[u32], member: &[u8],
         seen: &mut [u8], next: &mut Vec<u32>, alpha: usize) {
    let out_edges: usize = frontier.iter()
        .map(|&u| g.degree(u)).sum();
    let remaining = g.unvisited_edge_count(seen);
    if out_edges > remaining / alpha {
        g.pull_until_first_witness(member, seen, next);
    } else {
        g.push_unseen(frontier, seen, next);
    }
}
```

alpha is positive. Helpers are correct, current-frontier membership is fixed during a level, and next contains newly discovered vertices exactly once. The remaining-edge computation, frontier conversions, resets, and every failed pull probe are part of the cost. The baseline has a real algorithmic advantage on dense frontiers; the task is to make its worst-case work claim defensible without discarding that advantage.

Construct a budgeted hybrid that has O(n+m) total primitive work for every admitted graph in a sequential reference execution, including initialization and all conversions. A pull attempt may abort and finish the same level using push, retaining correct discoveries. Define precisely what consumes the budget: unvisited-vertex tests, adjacency probes, membership accesses, bookkeeping, and reset work cannot be hidden. Give explicit constants in an upper bound in your chosen primitive model, rather than only a measured average. No free oracle supplies the number of undiscovered edges.

The implementation must complete at least one nontrivial pull phase on an infinite family of dense graphs and perform asymptotically fewer adjacency probes on that family than a push-only query, excluding the separately charged graph build. For asymptotic statements, n and m vary in a word-RAM with sufficient index width; the stated limits bound the reference executable. Thus a program that always selects push does not meet the contract. A complete bipartite family is available as a test, but you must derive the source/frontier behavior and charge failed earlier speculation.

Provide an at-most-64-worker implementation with disjoint or synchronized discovery state, bounded local buffers, and a proof of its extra work term in workers and BFS levels. State scheduling assumptions for progress; no machine-time bound is required under arbitrary descheduling. Auxiliary storage is O(n+P) words plus a fixed-size buffer per worker, excluding CSR. Whole-array clearing on every level is unacceptable unless it is paid inside the claimed bound. Distances and parent edges must stay correct when pull discovers part of a level before fallback push begins.

Emit a certificate/trace per level containing budget grants, charged events, discovered vertices, and frontier construction totals. An independent CPython 3.12.4 checker must validate the accounting and BFS result against separately written graph logic. Supply a general potential/charging proof for all inputs; exhaustive small graphs supplement it. Check adversarially ordered dense graphs, long thin components, many isolated vertices, and frontiers whose samples overpredict success.

Inspect the linked push, pull, membership-maintenance, and parallel-discovery code. Map charged operations to finite machine-code paths, identify synchronization or bounds-check overhead absent from the abstract unit cost, and profile stalled loads and imbalance by level. Deliver code, checker, constructive dense-family witness, universal work proof, resource bound, and model-versus-hardware comparison. Optimization is assessed against the proved hybrid class, not against all possible BFS algorithms or every hardware schedule.

# 858. An Exact Residual Certificate for a Singular Landmark Block

Use OCaml 5.2 for a marginal-prior producer and Python 3.12 for an independent exact checker. The task is one frozen linearized bundle-adjustment window, not a nonlinear solver. Its objective is E(m, r)=1/2 ||J_m m+J_r r-b||², with at most 96 residual rows, 18 eliminated landmark coordinates m and 18 retained pose coordinates r. Every input entry is a rational multiple of 1/16 in [-4,4]. J_m may be rank deficient because landmarks have insufficient parallax or repeated observations; no damping, hidden prior or numerical rank threshold is part of the objective. Empty eliminated or retained blocks are admitted.

The producer must return a reduced residual representation A r-y and an affine eliminated-state representative m_star(r)=K r+k satisfying, for every rational m, r, E(m, r)=1/2||A r-y||²+1/2||J_m(m-m_star(r))||². It must also report a basis for the eliminated nullspace and describe which retained directions have zero reduced information. A and y may retain up to 96 rows; they need not be a square Cholesky factor. This allowance is intentional: the output is required to have rational entries even when a minimal square-root factor would require irrational numbers.

```ocaml
let marginalize jm jr b =
  let hmm = transpose jm *@ jm in
  let hmr = transpose jm *@ jr in
  let hrr = transpose jr *@ jr in
  let gm = transpose jm *- b in
  let gr = transpose jr *- b in
  for i = 0 to rows hmm - 1 do
    if abs_float hmm.(i).(i) < 1e-8 then hmm.(i).(i) <- 1e-8
  done;
  let inv = inverse hmm in
  let h = hrr -@ (transpose hmr *@ inv *@ hmr) in
  let g = gr -- (transpose hmr *- (inv *- gm)) in
  cholesky h, g
```

Operators and dense numeric helpers above have conventional matrix dimensions and are supplied otherwise correct. Construct a rank-deficient parallax fixture where this route changes the objective, produces an unusable square root or falsely claims information. Distinguish an explicitly regularized model from the unregularized elimination required here. Show why a pseudoinverse symbol alone is not an executable certificate of exact rank or of the reported prior.

Design a producer using rank factorization, exact elimination, orthogonal projectors represented rationally, or another finite algebraic route. Its certificate must include enough identities for the checker to verify the residual-energy decomposition, complete nullspaces and affine representative without rerunning the producer's pivot choices. Supply a rational right-inverse or reconstruction witness where needed. Verify equality as polynomial matrix identities for all m, r, rather than only at a handful of vectors. Rank-zero, full-rank and duplicated-column cases require explicit outputs.

Keep live memory below 32 MiB, counting all arbitrary-precision numerators/denominators, pivot tables, certificate buffers, native copies and one old prior still owned by a reader. Derive a finite bound on integer growth from the fixed dimensions and input denominator; an unbounded symbolic package allocation is not a resource proof. A binary64 fast path may propose a result, but exact validation and an exact fallback are required. Charge both in the reported cost.

The native interface uses contiguous row-major double matrices only for proposals; the authoritative certificate serializes signed integer numerators and positive denominators with explicit dimensions, variable IDs and tangent anchor. Inspect ABI offsets and one actual allocation or integer-size trace. Build an independent checker plus mutations changing rank, one cross term and one variable ID. Deliver one nontrivial singular-window certificate and show that all mutations fail. The strongest allowed claim is exact preservation of this frozen least-squares objective and its unobservable directions, without recovering discarded nonlinear measurements or interpreting a numerical regularizer as observed geometry.

# 861. A Four-Instruction Byte-Routing Fallback and Certificates of Minimality

Use Python 3.12 for synthesis/checking and GNU assembler 2.42 for AVX2 x86-64 code, Linux System V. A specialization receives a fixed permutation P of 0..31 and must implement out[j]=in[P[j]] on one 32-byte vector. Inputs are arbitrary bytes. The following generator creates two control vectors for an already short universal fallback; it sends same-lane and opposite-lane bytes through separate routes:

```python
def controls(P):
    assert sorted(P) == list(range(32))
    same = [0x80] * 32
    other = [0x80] * 32
    for j, k in enumerate(P):
        if (j // 16) == (k // 16):
            same[j] = k & 15
        else:
            other[j ^ 16] = k & 15
    return bytes(same), bytes(other)
```

```asm
# ymm0=input, ymm4=same control, ymm5=other control
vpshufb   ymm1,ymm0,ymm4
vpshufb   ymm2,ymm0,ymm5
vperm2i128 ymm2,ymm2,ymm2,0x01
vpor      ymm0,ymm1,ymm2
```

A synthesis timeout is not a minimality certificate. Programs using instructions outside this grammar may be reported as empirical controls only.

Design a symbolic representation that is complete even when an intermediate OR combines several distinct source bytes and a later shuffle discards that result. Do not assume without proof that every intermediate is itself a permutation. Explain why equivalence of the symbolic representation implies equivalence for all 2^256 runtime vectors. The generator/checker source should fit within 3000 nonblank lines, use at most 16 GiB offline memory, and emit at most ten live vector registers including constants. # 862. DTLS Handshake Fragments, Transcripts, and Record Acknowledgments

Implement a DTLS 1.3 handshake reassembler and flight ledger using Rust 1.85.1, with an independent Python checker. RFC 9147 defines message_seq, fragment offsets, transcript representation, and ACK meaning. Record deprotection is a supplied function returning authenticated immutable plaintext for an exact connection generation and record number. The exercise does not implement key exchange or certificate validation. Its handshake driver supplies the expected message types and permits the four messages in the fixture; connection IDs and the later return-routability extension are not negotiated. All fragment and ACK fixtures use authenticated epoch 2 records; epoch 1, post-handshake KeyUpdate, and message-sequence wrap are excluded.

The following kernel receives a fully parsed fragment. `off`, `len`, and total are decoded unsigned 24-bit fields; slices and ordinary overflow checks in the wrapper are assumed safe. `filled` is intended to indicate reassembly completeness.

```rust
fn fragment(s: &mut State, f: Fragment) {
    let completed = {
        let m = s.messages.entry(f.message_seq)
            .or_insert_with(|| Message::new(f.kind, f.total));
        m.body[f.off .. f.off + f.bytes.len()].copy_from_slice(&f.bytes);
        m.filled += f.bytes.len();
        if m.filled >= m.body.len() { Some(m.body.clone()) } else { None }

        s.transcript.extend_from_slice(&f.encoded_dtls_header);
        s.transcript.extend_from_slice(&body);
        s.deliver(f.message_seq, body);

}
```

# 868. Reproducible Sampling across Python Task Schedules

Use CPython 3.13.2 and asyncio. Three image jobs each contain four signed 16 samples and an explicitly supplied nonzero 32-bit seed.
```python
import asyncio
import contextvars

env_var = contextvars.ContextVar("sampler", default={
    "rng": 1, "scratch": [0,0,0,0]
})

def next32(env):
    x = env["rng"]
    x ^= (x << 13) & 0xffffffff
    x ^= x >> 17
    x ^= (x << 5) & 0xffffffff
    env["rng"] = x & 0xffffffff
    return env["rng"]

async def sample_job(frame_id, seed, samples, gate):
    env = env_var.get()
    env["scratch"][:] = samples
    chosen, score = [], 0
    for draw in range(3):
        await gate(frame_id, draw)
        index = next32(env) & 3
        chosen.append(index)
        score += env["scratch"][index]
    return frame_id, chosen, score
```

# 869. A Rank-and-Select Index Whose Saved Bits Must Also Save Dependent Misses

Use C++20, GCC 14.2 and base SVE on Neoverse N2 and Fujitsu A64FX. An immutable bit vector has n bits, where n is a multiple of 4,096 and `2^16 <= n <= 2^28`. Bits are packed low bit first in a 64-byte-aligned array of uint64 words. `rank(p)` counts set bits in `[0,p)`, including p=n; `select(k)` returns the position of the zero-based kth set bit, for valid k. The existing representation adds a rank9-style directory: one absolute count and seven packed 9-bit within-block counts for every 512 data bits.

```cpp
#include <bit>
#include <cstdint>
struct Meta { uint64_t base, sub; };
uint64_t rank9(const uint64_t* bits, const Meta* m,
               uint64_t n, uint64_t total, uint64_t p) {
    if (p==n) return total;
    uint64_t w=p>>6, b=w>>3, j=w&7, r=m[b].base;
    if (j) r += (m[b].sub>>(9*(j-1))) & 511;
    unsigned off=unsigned(p&63);
    if (off) r += std::popcount(bits[w]&((uint64_t(1)<<off)-1));
    return r;
}
// Existing select first upper-bounds the directory bases by k,
// then scans the chosen block's eight word counts and selects in one word.
unsigned select_word(uint64_t x, unsigned k) {
    while (k) { x &= x-1; --k; }
    return std::countr_zero(x); // precondition: k originally < popcount(x)
}
```

# 872. A Sparse Product Must Outgrow Its Fast Hash Table without Losing Determinism

Use CUDA C++17, CUDA 12.4.1, and H100 `sm_90`. Multiply two CSR matrices over integers modulo `2^32`, with dimension n<=4096 and at most `2^20` stored entries in each. The following insertion is bounded; if any insertion fails, the complete provisional row is discarded and recomputed by a correct slower fallback. No failed row is partially published.

```cpp
bool placed=false;
for (unsigned probe=0; probe<256; ++probe) {
  unsigned old=atomicCAS(&keys[h],EMPTY,col);
  if (old==EMPTY || old==col) {
```

# 878. Reconstructing an Alignment after the Bit-Parallel Distance Has Discarded Its Path

Use OCaml 4.07.1 native code on an AMD Zen 3 x86-64 core. The baseline below computes global unit-cost Levenshtein distance when the pattern has 1 through 63 bytes. `peq[c]` has bit i set exactly when pattern byte i equals c; its 256 entries are precomputed. The loop is already a word-parallel dynamic program, not a scalar matrix recurrence.

```ocaml
let distance63 peq m text =
  let open Int64 in
  let vp = ref minus_one and vn = ref zero in
  let score = ref m and top = shift_left one (m-1) in
  for j = 0 to String.length text - 1 do
    let eq = peq.(Char.code text.[j]) in
    let xv = logor eq !vn in
    let xh = logor (logxor (add (logand eq !vp) !vp) !vp) eq in
    let ph = logor !vn (lognot (logor xh !vp)) in
    let mh = logand !vp xh in
    if logand ph top <> zero then incr score;
    if logand mh top <> zero then decr score;
    let ph = logor (shift_left ph 1) one in
    let mh = shift_left mh 1 in
    vp := logor mh (lognot (logor xv ph));
    vn := logand ph xv
  done;
  !score
```
